Technology Briefing · The Hill Report
## Computing Power Is Ranked on a 64-Bit Benchmark
The supercomputer list counts double-precision operations on one dense problem, AI hardware is quoted in smaller number formats, and quantum machines now face a separate federal test that named its final-stage entrants on October 7.
Connor Hill · InsightfulWord · October 15
Key points| |
---
On October 7, Atom Computing, Diraq, IBM and IonQ were reported as advancing to **Stage C** of the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, which asks whether an industrially useful quantum computer can be built by **2033**.
|
---
The TOP500 supercomputer list ranks machines on a single benchmark that requires full **64-bit** arithmetic. The June 2026 leader, LineShine in Shenzhen, measured **2,198.40 petaflops**.
|
---
Hardware specification sheets quote several number formats side by side. One rack-scale system lists **1,440 petaflops** at 4-bit precision with sparsity and **2.88 petaflops** at 64-bit.
|
---
Energy efficiency has its own ranking. The current Green500 leader posts **73.282 gigaflops per watt**.
A computing figure without its benchmark and its number format is half a sentence. The same rack of hardware can be described with numbers that differ by a factor of several hundred, and every one of them is accurate for the format it names.
That is why the public rankings fix their rules in advance, and why the federal government built a separate test for quantum machines rather than borrowing one. This week the quantum test moved into its last stage.
On the tape| Oct 7Atom Computing, Diraq, IBM and IonQ were selected for Stage C of the Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, according to company releases and trade reports; three disclosed ceilings of up to $300 million each, and IBM did not disclose a figure.Why it matters: Stage C is the verification stage, in which the government works with each company to test whether its design can be built.
---
Oct 7The Department of Energy committed more than $500 million over five years, including exascale supercomputing, to a $1.8 billion virtual biology data initiative led by Biohub and the National Institutes of Health.Why it matters: federal computing support often arrives as machine time on national laboratory systems rather than as cash.
---
Oct 6Google and Constellation announced agreements covering about 3.6 gigawatts in the PJM region, including an 890-megawatt, 20-year nuclear power purchase agreement.Why it matters: large computing builds are now announced in megawatts as often as in operations per second.
---
Oct 5The Karlsruhe Institute of Technology described its new HoreKa 2 system, built with about 300 GB200 accelerators for €17 million, as having a "peak performance of 33 petaflops."Why it matters: a peak figure is a theoretical ceiling, and the announcement did not state the number format behind it.
---
Oct 2Oak Ridge National Laboratory reported that an algorithm run on its Frontier supercomputer cut the gate count of a quantum circuit from about 2,000,000 to 91,000.Why it matters: classical supercomputers already do part of the engineering work for quantum ones.
---
---
What the TOP500 Actually Measures
The TOP500 list has been compiled twice a year since 1993. Every entry runs the same benchmark, known as HPL or Linpack, which solves a large dense system of linear equations. The rules are strict: the operation count must be two-thirds of n cubed plus lower-order terms, and any method that computes the solution "in a precision lower than full 64-bit floating-point arithmetic" is excluded.
Two figures appear for each system. Rmax is the best performance actually measured on the benchmark. Rpeak is the theoretical peak, calculated from clock speeds and core counts. The ranking uses Rmax.
The June 2026 list, the 67th, put a new system first. LineShine, at the National Supercomputing Center in Shenzhen, measured an Rmax of 2,198.40 petaflops against an Rpeak of 2,735.82, drawing 42,220 kilowatts. The measured figure is about 80% of the peak; that ratio varies by architecture and is one reason the two columns are printed separately. It uses processors alone, with 13,789,440 cores, and the list's editors called it "the first China-based system to lead the TOP500 since Sunway TaihuLight in 2017."
Below it sit El Capitan at 1,809 petaflops, Frontier at 1,353, Aurora at 1,012 and Europe's JUPITER Booster at 1,000. One petaflop is a quadrillion operations per second; an exaflop is a thousand petaflops.
By the numbers
---
2,198.40| LineShine's measured petaflops on 64-bit HPL, June 2026
2,735.82| Its theoretical peak, the Rpeak column
42,220| Kilowatts drawn by LineShine during the run
1,440| Petaflops one rack lists at 4-bit precision with sparsity
2.88| Petaflops the same rack lists at 64-bit precision
73.282| Gigaflops per watt for the Green500 leader
---
The Same Machine at Lower Precision
Modern accelerators are built to work in several number formats. Lower precision means fewer bits per number, which means more operations per clock cycle and per watt. Neural network training and inference tolerate small formats well; physics simulations generally do not.
A current vendor specification for a 72-accelerator rack shows the spread. It lists 1,440 petaflops in a 4-bit format with sparsity, 720 at 8-bit, 360 at 16-bit, 180 at TF32 and 2.88 petaflops at 64-bit. A footnote adds that dense figures are "one-half sparse spec shown." Every number on that sheet is the same hardware.
The benchmark community has a measured bridge between the two worlds. HPL-MxP solves the same kind of problem but performs the heavy factorization in low precision, then uses iterative refinement to recover 64-bit accuracy in the answer. On the June results, El Capitan scored 16.7 exaflops on HPL-MxP, about 9.2 times its standard HPL score. LineShine, a processor-only machine, scored 7.92 exaflops, about 3.6 times.
Efficiency gets its own list. The Green500 reorders HPL results by gigaflops per watt. In June it was led by KAIROS, at the University of Toulouse and the national research center CNRS in France, at 73.282, a small 3.05-petaflop system drawing 46 kilowatts. LineShine runs at 52.07.
| 📌 Fresh Signal4The number of companies reported on October 7 as advancing to Stage C of the Quantum Benchmarking Initiative: Atom Computing, Diraq, IBM and IonQ. Trade reports add that Microsoft and PsiQuantum were already in that stage through an earlier pilot program. Stage C is where the government verifies and validates whether each design can actually be constructed.
---|---
---
How a Federal Program Benchmarks Quantum Machines
Quantum computers are not ranked on HPL. The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency built its own process instead. Its stated aim is to "determine whether it's possible to build an industrially-useful computer by 2033" and to "rigorously verify and validate whether any quantum computing approach can achieve utility-scale operation." The agency describes the program as "not a competition." Selection rests on written submissions and oral presentations reviewed by government teams, not on a common speed score.
It runs in three stages. In Stage A, companies describe a utility-scale concept; seventeen were named in April 2025. In Stage B, they present a research and development plan; eleven were listed by November 2025. In Stage C, each works with the government to verify that its design can be built. Funding is stated as ceilings, and IonQ's release notes that amounts beyond the first obligation depend on future appropriations.
Other federal money arrives through different channels with different terms. On May 21, 2026, the Commerce Department issued letters of intent to nine quantum firms totaling $2.013 billion, each conditioned on the department receiving a non-controlling minority equity stake. Letters of intent become binding only when definitive agreements are signed; D-Wave reported its definitive agreement, for up to $100 million, on September 8.
The Energy Department is taking a third route. Its Genesis Q competition sets prize pools for systems reaching 100, 150 and 200 logical qubits, and applications are due October 19. Of the up to $215 million planned, $2.5 million is in fiscal 2026 dollars; the rest depends on appropriations.
Where performance figures are published
---
TOP500| Measured and peak 64-bit HPL resultsTwice a year; June 2026 was the 67th list
Green500| HPL results per wattKAIROS leads at 73.282 gigaflops per watt
HPL-MxP| Mixed-precision solve refined to 64-bit accuracyEl Capitan 16.7 exaflops
Quantum Benchmarking Initiative| Stages A, B and C toward a 2033 questionStage C entrants reported October 7
One question for the deskWhen a computing figure appears in a headline, which detail gets checked first — the number format, the power draw or the benchmark name?Hit reply — one line is enough.
---
Worth stating plainlySupercomputer rankings use one benchmark at full 64-bit precision, and they report a measured figure separately from a theoretical peak. AI hardware is quoted in several smaller formats that produce larger numbers from the same chips. Quantum machines are assessed through a staged federal program, and federal quantum funding is expressed as ceilings, letters of intent and equity stakes, each with its own conditions.
---
The short checklist| 1.| Find the number format attached to any flops figure: 64-bit, 16-bit, 8-bit or 4-bit.
---|---
2.| Separate a measured result from a theoretical peak; the TOP500 prints both.
---|---
3.| Check whether an accelerator figure assumes sparsity, which doubles the quoted rate.
---|---
4.| Read power draw beside performance, and look up the Green500 for efficiency.
---|---
5.| For quantum programs, note the stage reached and whether funding is obligated or a ceiling.
---|---
6.| For federal awards, distinguish a letter of intent from a signed definitive agreement.
---|---
---
Replies to this briefing reach a person, not a queue.Connor Hill reads every reply.
Sources checked
Verified October 07, 2026
TOP500, project description, Linpack rules, and the June 2026 TOP500 and Green500 lists
Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency, Quantum Benchmarking Initiative program pages and Stage A and Stage B announcements
Quantum Computing Report and IonQ, Stage C selections, October 7, 2026
National Institute of Standards and Technology, CHIPS quantum letters of intent release, May 21, 2026
NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 specifications, and HPL-MxP benchmark description
Department of Energy, Genesis Q competition notice, September 17, 2026; Data Center Dynamics on HoreKa 2 and the Google–Constellation agreements

body:
No te dejes, Peter. We’re winning this fight.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Hi Peter, it’s Gina.
Exactly one year ago today, we launched this campaign.
For the first few months of this campaign, I was totally written off — no one believed we could beat a three-term incumbent. I was a state representative with very little statewide name recognition, and early polls showed us down 10 points.
**Today, because of supporters like you, this has grown into one of the strongest, most competitive campaigns in the _entire country_.** We have wiped out that 10-point deficit and are now leading Greg Abbott in five polls. Together, we’ve built an incredible grassroots coalition powered by over 475,000 unique online contributions and more than 250,000 individual donors who believe in a better Texas.
I want to thank you for following our journey and being part of this movement, Peter. body:
Supporting Susan = Saving Maine

Dear Peter,If you tuned into CNBC’s Squawk Box, you heard something important. Former Senator Joe Manchin didn’t hold back when talking about what’s at stake in this election:“If you lose Susan Collins in the Senate, you are losing the soul of the Senate.”
---
| [CLICK HERE TO WATCH THE FULL VIDEO](https://trk.emails.susancollinsformaine.-DHPjiiuMVx6bJAQWZbR1w)
---
Joe knows better than almost anyone what it takes to get real work done in a divided Capitol. And he knows that Susan isn’t interested in soundbites, political games, or partisan theater.She is in the trenches for you every single day, fighting for Maine’s working families, delivering real results for our local communities, and serving as the steady, independent voice our country desperately needs.When Washington grows more polarized, Susan stands firm. She never stops fighting for Maine, and she never forgets who sent her to work.Losing Susan’s voice in the Senate isn't an option, not for Maine, and not for the country.
---
| [CHIP IN TO SUPPORT THE SOUL OF THE SENATE](https://trk.emails.susancollinsformaine.)
---
Thank you for standing with Susan today.
Team Collins

Peter,
On Monday, federal agents searched Congresswoman Ilhan Omar’s home — just three weeks before Americans head to the polls.
**Americans see this for what it is: President Trump is abusing his power to go after his political opponents in the final weeks before voters have their say.**
I’ve been on the receiving end of this myself. Earlier this year, Trump’s Justice Department came after me and other Minnesota leaders for standing up to ICE’s abuses in our communities. A federal judge threw out their subpoenas, finding they were intended to _“harass, coerce, and retaliate.”_
That tells you a whole lot about how this administration operates. Stand up to them, and they’ll use every lever of power they have to try to silence you.
We need to stand with Ilhan. And we need to back that up with real support for her campaign and the Democrats fighting to hold this administration accountable.
**[Will you split a donation of $5 between Ilhan Omar’s campaign and Small Town PAC today? Let’s have Ilhan’s back and help elect more Democrats who refuse to be bullied into silence.](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261015-partner-io.xshRe5&amount=5&refcode=em20261015-1212&t=1&akid=1212%2E34582%2EfFVauv)**
Look, the damage here goes well beyond any one of us. It’s the message this sends to anybody thinking about speaking out: Keep your head down. Don’t challenge the people in charge. Don’t be next.
We cannot let that work.

Tim Walz

body:
Should elected officials refuse lobbyist and PAC money? Share your opinion—and watch the debate October 29 at 7 PM on News 8.
Watch me debate Joe Morelle October 29 at 7 PM on News 8. Reply and tell me what matters most to you.
|

[ ](https://52zrz7fk.r.us-east-1.awstrack.me/L0/https:%2F%2Ftracking.virginiamcintyreforcongress.com%2F%-f0810bff-d7bb-4b36-b76a-ac718a8b59c6-000000/I4mldUw-BBM0CpxiOGIl1AflAFs=473)
# Watch the Congressional Debate
Thursday, October 29
7 PM on News 8 Dear Neighbor, Big-money politics is dividing America, and too many people feel their voices are being drowned out. I am running for Congress because our community deserves a representative who listens and puts your concerns first. I refuse to accept money from lobbyists, PACs, and even the Republican National Committee. My commitment is to you, and I invite you to join our movement to bring an independent voice to Washington.
On **Thursday, October 29, at 7 PM on News 8** , I will debate **Joe Morelle** and share my priorities for our community. I hope you will tune in, hear where we stand, and encourage your friends and family to watch.
[ ](https://52zrz7fk.r.us-east-1.awstrack.me/L0/https:%2F%2Ftracking.virginiamcintyreforcongress.com%2F%-f0810bff-d7bb-4b36-b76a-ac718a8b59c6-000000/tXM7hEs_39w3zn2hHDCDJAASw5w=473)
## A Proven Record of Putting Our Community First
I believe good ideas should come before party labels. My approach is simple: listen to people, study the facts, and make decisions based on what serves our community. That is the same commitment I will bring to Washington. **I would be honored to earn your vote and serve as an independent voice for Monroe and Ontario Counties.**
| [Visit My Website](https://52zrz7fk.r.us-east-1.awstrack.me/L0/https:%2F%2Ftracking.virginiamcintyreforcongress.com%2F%-f0810bff-d7bb-4b36-b76a-ac718a8b59c6-000000/qiP5nZ-XYrz5AG_Af8nYPrA42bg=473)

As I prepare for the debate, I want to hear from you. **What matters most to you and your family? What would you like me to discuss?** Please reply directly to this email and share your priorities. As head of the U.S. Department of Justice for six years, I saw firsthand that the people who righteously stand up to protect families from the bad actors trying to take advantage of them are rarely just in Washington. They're state attorneys general. They're governors.
I've watched Aaron Ford fight to protect the everyday person in Nevada for years now, and I can tell you that he’s the real deal. I know Aaron is someone who has used the law to protect people instead of protecting power, and I know he will continue to do so.
**Now, as Aaron steps up to take on MAGA Gov. Joe Lombardo and move Nevada forward, I’m thrilled to give him my full endorsement. I know Aaron will be an outstanding governor for Nevadans.**
**[Before I say more, will you chip in $5 right now to help elect Aaron this November? The polls show this race is neck-and-neck, and Aaron needs all of us to pitch in to get him across the finish line.](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20261015_1_ak.VB2e4L&amount=5&refcode=em20261015-1082&t=4&akid=1082%2E127862%2ElheHMv)**

Aaron’s work has delivered _real_ results for Nevadans.
MAGA Gov. Joe Lombardo, on the other hand, uses his position of power to cheer on Trump and prioritize his donors’ profits over Nevadans’ wellbeing. Recently, Lombardo took millions from mega donors who are profiting from building dozens of data centers across Nevada.
And that’s just _one_ example of how corrupt Lombardo’s priorities are.
Thankfully, we have an opportunity to defeat Lombardo this November and elect a true fighter in his place: **Aaron Ford.**
This race matters far beyond Nevada's state lines. **As the Trump administration works to weaken voting protections nationwide, Nevada is one of the best chances Democrats have anywhere in the country to flip a governor's seat blue in 2026 — and put a governor in office who'll defend fair elections instead of undermining them.**
But Aaron is counting on grassroots support to compete with Lombardo’s billionaire backers. **[So please, will you help Aaron win this toss-up race with a $5 donation today?](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20261015_1_ak.VB2e4L&amount=5&refcode=em20261015-1082&t=24&akid=1082%2E127862%2ElheHMv)**

name: Voto Latino
subject: Texas has the chance to flip blue this November
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Voto Latino
body:
For the first time in three decades.
#
Peter,
**Texas is closer than it’s been in _three decades_ to flipping blue, and Latino voters could be the reason it finally happens.**
With Gina Hinojosa running for Governor and James Talarico running for the U.S. Senate, we have a **once-in-a-generation** opportunity to break decades of one-party rule and bring real leadership to Texas.
**But Republicans are working overtime to make sure our voices aren’t heard.**
It’s the reason why Texas has purged over 1.2 million voters from the rolls. It’s why Republicans have passed law after law, making it harder to register, harder to vote, and harder for Latino communities to participate and make their voices heard in November.
They can’t win in a fair fight against furious and energized Latino voters, so they’re trying to shrink it before November.
Right now, Voto Latino is on the ground — reaching voters, countering misinformation, and making sure every eligible Latino voter in Texas has what they need to show up on Election Day.

Democratic U.S. Senate nominee Troy Jackson blamed an alleged $40,000 extortion attempt and investigative reporting by The Maine Wire for the loss of his lawyer, missed court deadlines and the dismissal of a lawsuit he and his second cousin filed.
The then-Senate president made the extortion allegations in an extraordinary letter dated May 6, 2024, asking Superior Court Justice Michaela Murphy to keep his case alive even though she had dismissed it with prejudice in April.
"We feel like the opposing lawyer tried to extort us for $40,000 or face public humiliation," Jackson wrote. "When we refused, the humiliation did come, but more than anything it took our lawyer and any legal cohesion we had in the case."
The correspondence, obtained by The Maine Wire, shows how Jackson tried to salvage a lawsuit that exposed his own financial dealings to scrutiny, years before his bid to unseat Republican U.S. Sen. Susan Collins. The unusual letter succeeded in getting Murphy to reverse her earlier decision, but Jackson and his second cousin eventually agreed to drop the case.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c128e1cb-3585-4404-b40d-d2028c4a13ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Jackson and his [second cousin, Lana Pelletier](https://substack.com/redirect/11438f50-11d8-43ab-84ae-345d5f10ef99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), bought the Augusta house from Paul and Jane Godbout for $216,000 in September 2019. They sued in June 2020, alleging the sellers concealed carpenter ant damage, mold and other defects. The Godbouts denied wrongdoing and produced evidence that they had paid for the buyers' home inspection.
Court records examined for The Maine Wire's [August 2023 reporting](https://substack.com/redirect/4e4b8e96-64cd-4bad-b148-0befd69696dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) showed the inspection warned of carpenter ants and recommended a pest specialist. Jackson and Pelletier received the report but did not hire the specialist. In the lawsuit, they claimed they were blindsided by the carpenter ant damage.
Jackson and Pelletier sold the house for $323,000 in December 2021, $107,000 more than they paid. They kept suing.
The Maine Wire's reporting also examined Jackson's federally insured mortgage. Under the terms of his Federal Housing Administration (FHA) loan, he was required to make the Augusta house his principal residence within 60 days and keep it that way for at least a year.
That conflicted with his constitutional requirement to abide at the Aroostook County address listed in his campaign finance filings.
"This is unfortunate, but I never really read the forms," Jackson [told the Portland Press Herald](https://substack.com/redirect/65422f7d-d579-40fe-989d-9c92d177899c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in September 2023.
Throughout the ensuing ethics imbroglio, Jackson maintained that Allagash remained his legal home and that the Augusta property was for legislative work. His account, which has changed according to the location and audience, has raised questions about whether he ever intended to fulfill the mortgage's occupancy requirement.
On the campaign trail, Jackson has described the house as little more than a place to keep his clothes. During an [October debate against Collins](https://substack.com/redirect/7f67c4e3-4d69-4c09-9b4d-5abbcbbd7d97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), when Maine's senior senator raised questions about the FHA loan, he said he stayed at the house five days a week during the legislative session.
Jackson has not been charged with a crime in connection with the mortgage.
In his 2024 letter to the court, Jackson said the Godbouts' lawyer raised the mortgage problem two years before the reporting appeared:
> "For more clarity, the lawyer representing the Godbouts sent us a letter in 2021 saying that I had violated HUD law when we applied for a loan. He said the home we were purchasing could not be my primary home, because as a State Senator for District #1 my home had to be in northern Aroostook County. He said that if we paid them $40,000 and dropped the case then he wouldn't go to the media. We refused immediately and told them to go to the media."
(For clarity, the lawyer would have had no reason to suspect that Jackson had violated "HUD law," as opposed to violating his constitutional obligation to remain a resident of the district he was representing in the State Senate.)
Jackson did not identify the attorney by name in his letter to Murphy. Jed Davis and Jennifer Bryant, both of Jim Mitchell & Jed Davis, P.A., represented the Godbouts during the litigation.
In the letter and related court records reviewed for this story, Jackson did not supply any evidence of the alleged 2021 extortion attempt.
The defense called Jackson's allegations "false and irrelevant."
Jackson had not raised the alleged demand in the public responses when The Maine Wire first broke the story or in subsequent media coverage. Indeed, the letter is the only instance in which Jackson has claimed that he was the victim of extortion.
His letter lamented the loss of Preti Flaherty attorney Matthew Warner, who represented the couple on a contingency-fee basis. Warner's fee depended on Jackson and Pelletier recovering money, which means Jackson's legal representation -- up until The Maine Wire exposed the lawsuit -- was effectively free.
Preti Flaherty, among Maine's largest legal and lobbying firms, also previously employed [Chace Jackson](https://substack.com/redirect/452e8288-4e63-4fe6-ad7f-1f82a3454e69?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), one of Jackson and Pelletier's two sons, as a legislative liaison.
Jackson claimed, without providing any evidence, the Godbouts' lawyer later fed publicly available mortgage information to "Republican" news outlets. He then explained why he believed his own firm had abandoned him:
> "The political hit piece was tough, but something I am used to dealing with. What I was not ready for was some of the circle of political foes filing ethics complaints against me. These complaints were all ruled unanimously in my favor, but the law firm that my lawyer worked for had a government affairs arm to their firm and their legal team thought that it was not worth them risking attack by continuing to represent us. He was forced by his firm to withdraw from our case back in December."
Warner's withdrawal motion, quoted in the defense filing, gave a different account: "The plaintiffs have elected to represent themselves, without a lawyer, in this case moving forward." The records contain no statement from Preti confirming Jackson's claim of political pressure.
The ethics ruling was also narrower than Jackson's letter suggested.
The [October 2023 vote](https://substack.com/redirect/ea987599-81e5-474f-81b9-c1ef14549230?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) concerned a complaint by then-Rep. John Andrews, R-Paris, about Jackson's campaign address. Commissioners voted 5-0 to take no further action. The commission lacked authority to investigate the mortgage, insurance and legislative reimbursement allegations. Its vote did not clear Jackson of mortgage or insurance fraud.
After Warner withdrew, the court ordered Jackson and Pelletier to obtain another lawyer or report that they would represent themselves. They missed a Feb. 9 deadline, according to the defense. Bryant moved to dismiss Feb. 22, reporting more than $40,000 in defense fees and costs.
Murphy granted dismissal April 22.
Jackson, in the letter, blamed the missed deadlines on court correspondence he said never arrived after his lawyer withdrew. The court, he claimed, had continued sending notices to the Augusta house he and his second cousin had already sold.
"Apparently, withdrawing also meant not forwarding any of the Court documents or correspondence to us," Jackson wrote. He said he learned about a development in the case less than a month before writing his letter.
His letter listed a different Augusta address in type, with his claimed Allagash residence added by hand. The defendants disputed his account, saying notices had been mailed to Allagash, the address Jackson listed on campaign filings and claimed was his real home during Ethics Commission proceedings.
However, Jackson's bizarre letter, filled with unsubstantiated allegations and outright falsehoods, was convincing enough for Murphy to reverse her decision.
Murphy vacated the dismissal May 21, the same day the court received Jackson's letter. She said it raised questions about whether the plaintiffs had received important documents. She ordered a conference and directed the clerk to send defense counsel a copy.
Murphy, who handled Donald Trump's 2024 ballot-access case, was a [registered Democrat in November 2023](https://substack.com/redirect/28768532-e0f3-468d-b3f0-7f4a03708136?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), according to voting records cited by news outlets. She is also the mother of Henry Beck, the Democratic former state treasurer. Beck's role hosting a September 2026 fundraiser for Jackson drew criticism from campaign supporters over his [pro-Israel advocacy](https://substack.com/redirect/208e4fe6-6565-40af-9e4a-25cea24f023d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), according to Drop Site News.
The Godbouts' attorneys asked Murphy to reconsider, accusing Jackson of misleading the court. Their June filing quoted a Feb. 29 email from Warner that challenged Jackson's account of when he learned his case was in jeopardy:
> "Lana and Troy forwarded me a copy of a recent filing you made that referenced a court order from December."
In other words, Jackson's previous attorney claimed that Jackson and his second cousin had not only received the court records they later claimed not to have received, but they passed along those very documents to legal counsel.
Defense counsel said they sent Warner the orders that day. They argued the exchange showed Jackson knew about the dismissal effort months before the court received his letter. They also objected that Murphy reopened the case without giving them a chance to respond.
"The fault lies with Plaintiffs, not the Court," they wrote.
Jackson had asked for the chance to present his claims "win or lose."
On Aug. 30, 2024, he and Pelletier signed a stipulation dismissing the lawsuit "with prejudice and without costs to any party." Bryant signed for the defendants.
The document disclosed no separate settlement terms or payment.
It's unclear whether Jackson ever paid for his own attorney fees or the fees his lawsuit imposed on the Godbouts.

In latest chapter in Troy Jackson's litigious attempt to extract money from the couple who sold him and his second cousin an Augusta home in 2019, Jackson alleges he was the victim of extortion. Oct 15 | | | | | | | | | | | Democratic U.S. Senate nominee Troy Jackson blamed an alleged $40,000 extortion attempt and investigative reporting by The Maine Wire for the loss of his lawyer, missed court deadlines and the dismissal of a lawsuit he and his second cousin filed. The then-Senate president made the extortion allegations in an extraordinary letter dated May 6, 2024, asking Superior Court Justice Michaela Murphy to keep his case alive even though she had dismissed it with prejudice in April. "We feel like the opposing lawyer tried to extort us for $40,000 or face public humiliation," Jackson wrote. "When we refused, the humiliation did come, but more than anything it took our lawyer and any legal cohesion we had in the case." The correspondence, obtained by The Maine Wire, shows how Jackson tried to salvage a lawsuit that exposed his own financial dealings to scrutiny, years before his bid to unseat Republican U.S. Sen. Susan Collins. The unusual letter succeeded in getting Murphy to reverse her earlier decision, but Jackson and his second cousin eventually agreed to drop the case. | | ---|---|--- Jackson and his , bought the Augusta house from Paul and Jane Godbout for $216,000 in September 2019. They sued in June 2020, alleging the sellers concealed carpenter ant damage, mold and other defects. The Godbouts denied wrongdoing and produced evidence that they had paid for the buyers' home inspection. Court records examined for The Maine Wire's showed the inspection warned of carpenter ants and recommended a pest specialist. Jackson and Pelletier received the report but did not hire the specialist. In the lawsuit, they claimed they were blindsided by the carpenter ant damage. Jackson and Pelletier sold the house for $323,000 in December 2021, $107,000 more than they paid. They kept suing. The Maine Wire's reporting also examined Jackson's federally insured mortgage. Under the terms of his Federal Housing Administration (FHA) loan, he was required to make the Augusta house his principal residence within 60 days and keep it that way for at least a year. That conflicted with his constitutional requirement to abide at the Aroostook County address listed in his campaign finance filings. "This is unfortunate, but I never really read the forms," Jackson in September 2023. Throughout the ensuing ethics imbroglio, Jackson maintained that Allagash remained his legal home and that the Augusta property was for legislative work. His account, which has changed according to the location and audience, has raised questions about whether he ever intended to fulfill the mortgage's occupancy requirement. On the campaign trail, Jackson has described the house as little more than a place to keep his clothes. During an , when Maine's senior senator raised questions about the FHA loan, he said he stayed at the house five days a week during the legislative session. Jackson has not been charged with a crime in connection with the mortgage. In his 2024 letter to the court, Jackson said the Godbouts' lawyer raised the mortgage problem two years before the reporting appeared: "For more clarity, the lawyer representing the Godbouts sent us a letter in 2021 saying that I had violated HUD law when we applied for a loan. He said the home we were purchasing could not be my primary home, because as a State Senator for District #1 my home had to be in northern Aroostook County. He said that if we paid them $40,000 and dropped the case then he wouldn't go to the media. We refused immediately and told them to go to the media." (For clarity, the lawyer would have had no reason to suspect that Jackson had violated "HUD law," as opposed to violating his constitutional obligation to remain a resident of the district he was representing in the State Senate.) Jackson did not identify the attorney by name in his letter to Murphy. Jed Davis and Jennifer Bryant, both of Jim Mitchell & Jed Davis, P.A., represented the Godbouts during the litigation. In the letter and related court records reviewed for this story, Jackson did not supply any evidence of the alleged 2021 extortion attempt. The defense called Jackson's allegations "false and irrelevant." Jackson had not raised the alleged demand in the public responses when The Maine Wire first broke the story or in subsequent media coverage. Indeed, the letter is the only instance in which Jackson has claimed that he was the victim of extortion. His letter lamented the loss of Preti Flaherty attorney Matthew Warner, who represented the couple on a contingency-fee basis. Warner's fee depended on Jackson and Pelletier recovering money, which means Jackson's legal representation -- up until The Maine Wire exposed the lawsuit -- was effectively free. Preti Flaherty, among Maine's largest legal and lobbying firms, also previously employed , one of Jackson and Pelletier's two sons, as a legislative liaison. Jackson claimed, without providing any evidence, the Godbouts' lawyer later fed publicly available mortgage information to "Republican" news outlets. He then explained why he believed his own firm had abandoned him: "The political hit piece was tough, but something I am used to dealing with. What I was not ready for was some of the circle of political foes filing ethics complaints against me. These complaints were all ruled unanimously in my favor, but the law firm that my lawyer worked for had a government affairs arm to their firm and their legal team thought that it was not worth them risking attack by continuing to represent us. He was forced by his firm to withdraw from our case back in December." Warner's withdrawal motion, quoted in the defense filing, gave a different account: "The plaintiffs have elected to represent themselves, without a lawyer, in this case moving forward." The records contain no statement from Preti confirming Jackson's claim of political pressure. The ethics ruling was also narrower than Jackson's letter suggested. The concerned a complaint by then-Rep. John Andrews, R-Paris, about Jackson's campaign address. Commissioners voted 5-0 to take no further action. The commission lacked authority to investigate the mortgage, insurance and legislative reimbursement allegations. Its vote did not clear Jackson of mortgage or insurance fraud. After Warner withdrew, the court ordered Jackson and Pelletier to obtain another lawyer or report that they would represent themselves. They missed a Feb. 9 deadline, according to the defense. Bryant moved to dismiss Feb. 22, reporting more than $40,000 in defense fees and costs. Murphy granted dismissal April 22. Jackson, in the letter, blamed the missed deadlines on court correspondence he said never arrived after his lawyer withdrew. The court, he claimed, had continued sending notices to the Augusta house he and his second cousin had already sold. "Apparently, withdrawing also meant not forwarding any of the Court documents or correspondence to us," Jackson wrote. He said he learned about a development in the case less than a month before writing his letter. His letter listed a different Augusta address in type, with his claimed Allagash residence added by hand. The defendants disputed his account, saying notices had been mailed to Allagash, the address Jackson listed on campaign filings and claimed was his real home during Ethics Commission proceedings. However, Jackson's bizarre letter, filled with unsubstantiated allegations and outright falsehoods, was convincing enough for Murphy to reverse her decision. Murphy vacated the dismissal May 21, the same day the court received Jackson's letter. She said it raised questions about whether the plaintiffs had received important documents. She ordered a conference and directed the clerk to send defense counsel a copy. Murphy, who handled Donald Trump's 2024 ballot-access case, was a , according to voting records cited by news outlets. She is also the mother of Henry Beck, the Democratic former state treasurer. Beck's role hosting a September 2026 fundraiser for Jackson drew criticism from campaign supporters over his , according to Drop Site News. The Godbouts' attorneys asked Murphy to reconsider, accusing Jackson of misleading the court. Their June filing quoted a Feb. 29 email from Warner that challenged Jackson's account of when he learned his case was in jeopardy: "Lana and Troy forwarded me a copy of a recent filing you made that referenced a court order from December." In other words, Jackson's previous attorney claimed that Jackson and his second cousin had not only received the court records they later claimed not to have received, but they passed along those very documents to legal counsel. Defense counsel said they sent Warner the orders that day. They argued the exchange showed Jackson knew about the dismissal effort months before the court received his letter. They also objected that Murphy reopened the case without giving them a chance to respond. "The fault lies with Plaintiffs, not the Court," they wrote. Jackson had asked for the chance to present his claims "win or lose." On Aug. 30, 2024, he and Pelletier signed a stipulation dismissing the lawsuit "with prejudice and without costs to any party." Bryant signed for the defendants. The document disclosed no separate settlement terms or payment. It's unclear whether Jackson ever paid for his own attorney fees or the fees his lawsuit imposed on the Godbouts. Read more: You 're receiving The Robinson Report for free. clean_body: | | | | == | 19 Days To Go | | == 19 Days to Go I had a great conversation with Catie Beck on WTVR's Untold podcast. We talked about my journey from a tough childhood, through my time as a Navy SEAL, building a business, and now serving the people of Virginia's 5th District, and why I'm asking for the honor of continuing that service. Thank you, Catie, for the thoughtful discussion. I hope you'll take a few minutes to listen. == Please Vote Early | Maybe you've seen me at your church? My wife and I attend our church early on Sunday, and then I often visit a second or even a third service. Since 2017, I've worshipped at 411 different churches across the district, where I've received countless prayers, wisdom, and advice. I'm encouraging every churchgoer to vote after church this Sunday. Virginia early voting is open on weekdays through October 31, plus these remaining weekend days: Sunday, October 18 Saturday, October 24 Sunday, October 25 Saturday, October 31 Hours and locations vary by locality. Check your county registrar's office or visit ==. Bring a friend from church! Meet Majority Leader Steve Scalese In Lynchburg | Join me for a special event on Tuesday, October 20th at the home of Mike and Elizabeth Harrington in Lynchburg with my good friend, Majority Leader Steve Scalise. == Please remind your friends to vote: Re-elect John McGuire to Congress Bert Mizusawa for U.S. Senate What We've Delivered for Virginia's 5th District Since January 2025 Secured the border No tax on tips No tax on overtime No tax on social security Negotiated roughly $20 billion in investment, creating about 7,000 well-paying jobs Returned over $10 million owed by the federal government to constituents Passed the Wintergreen Emergency Egress Act (after 25+ years of failure), now through Senate committee unanimously Delivered a Navy and Marine Corps ROTC program at Liberty University (pursued since 1971) * Worked with Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth to help bring 57 constituents home from Israel during missile attacks My opponent voted for cap and trade to double your energy costs because he wants to end the use of fossil fuels, he worked for George Soros and funded open-border policies, is endorsed by Democratic Socialist AOC for supporting her agenda, and brags about being the deciding House vote for Obamacare, a program that doubled premiums and gave insurance companies a 2,000 percent pay raise. | More Perriello Lies | Many fell for Perriello's friend Abigail "bait and switch" Spanberger's lies. Don't fall for the "bait and switch" again. Perriello said he was pro life and pro gun and then in the governor primary he said he was not pro life and not pro gun. After his ridiculous insider trading lies about me, now Perriello has now accused me of supporting adult men marrying minors. That shows he is sick and it is false and once again proves Perriello, like Spanberger, will say or do anything to get your vote. Virginia law already required a judge's approval and included strong safeguards. These cases were rare. I did not believe Richmond politicians should override the judgment of parents and judges in those limited situations. Forty-two other lawmakers also voted no for the same reason. Some of those rare cases involved military families. A young man can enlist at 17 or 18 and deploy overseas. If he has a 17-year-old fiancee, marrying before he ships out is often the only way to ensure she receives full survivor benefits if he does not come home. We wanted families to have that option. As a father of five, I take a back seat to no one on protecting children, and neither does my record. Perriello Silent On Protecting Children | | | My opponent stayed silent for three months on the == Many constituents called me asking for help. They said there was an obvious cover-up and none of their representatives would answer the call. They needed an investigation to protect their children. On July 9 I sent a letter that sparked bipartisan support to Governor Spanberger demanding a full investigation. Spanberger's office responded about nine days later. Then Democrat Senator Creigh Deeds and Democrat Delegates Katrina Callsen and Amy Laufer joined the call. On July 18 I publicly invited Tom Perriello to stand with us. He said nothing for three months. Now he is finally making a comment after seeing the poll numbers. Protecting children should never take a back seat to politics. == | Kash Patel Joins McGuire in Lynchburg | | == | It was an honor to host a law enforcement round table with FBI Director Kash Patel at Liberty University in Lynchburg, Virginia. == On X Fake News Gets Caught Comments On The Kash Patel Visit == == == | No Valley Link On request from many constituents, I sent a letter to Governor Abigail Spanberger at the beginning of July 2026 on the 10th asking her administration to stop the Valley Link transmission line project due to constituent concerns about private property rights, farmland, and environmental impacts. == | Virginias Football Visits | | == | | == | | == | Ive had a lot of fun meeting and talking with constituents at college and high school football games. It's Chris.
**There are just 19 days left of this campaign, and we need all hands on deck.**
The GOP has pledged more than $60 million trying to buy this Senate seat.
I don't take a dime of corporate PAC money.
Our strength comes from people like you, and with time running out, we need to show John Sununu that New Hampshire isn't for sale.
**[Will you chip in $10 or whatever makes sense for you right now to help us beat Sununu, keep the Granite State blue, and flip the Senate?](https://substack.com/redirect/79ecf8f5-070f-439f-8b32-d4a0e13e6a2b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/79ecf8f5-070f-439f-8b32-d4a0e13e6a2b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**I know that in a race as critical as New Hampshire 's Senate seat, falling behind in fundraising simply isn't an option.**
This campaign was built from the ground up by supporters like you. We wouldn't be where we are today without people believing in our shared vision for a freer, fairer future.
But if we're going to defend this Senate seat and keep it out of the hands of John Sununu, we need everyone on this grassroots team to step up.
**[That's why today I'm lowering my ask to just $1 today.](https://substack.com/redirect/b14027c5-0f9c-41dc-b5e0-82e2a058adbd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[DONATE $1](https://substack.com/redirect/b14027c5-0f9c-41dc-b5e0-82e2a058adbd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A dollar may not seem like much on its own, but there are hundreds of thousands of supporters reading this message right now, _including you._ When everyone chips in together, even one dollar can make a huge impact.
Right now my opponent John Sununu's backed by the entire MAGA machine and they are outspending us three to one. We need all the resources we can get to fight back. We may not match them dollar for dollar, but as long as we get all the resources we need, we'll have what it takes to stay on track and win.
Everything we've accomplished comes down to the collective effort of this team -- from Granite Staters to supporters across the country who believe in commonsense leadership, protecting fundamental freedoms, and delivering for working families.
With a surge of support right now during these final weeks before Election Day, I know we can hold this seat and get one step closer to taking back the Senate.
**[Will you chip in just $1 today to keep our campaign on track?](https://substack.com/redirect/b14027c5-0f9c-41dc-b5e0-82e2a058adbd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ DONATE $1](https://substack.com/redirect/b14027c5-0f9c-41dc-b5e0-82e2a058adbd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you,
Chris

Early Vote Action

Today, I want to show you why your support matters so much. But first... When warriors go into battle, they know someone has their back. **But too many of them stand alone when the fight follows them home.** A police officer who made a split-second call... a soldier whose career was destroyed by bureaucracy... a veteran crushed by a political prosecution. Their careers vanish. Their savings disappear. Their families suffer. _All while the system they served turns on them._ **That 's where Pipe Hitter Foundation steps in.** We provide legal defense support... emergency financial help... and the resources these families need to survive the fight. **But none of this happens without patriots like you.** **And right now, I want to introduce you to a handful of warriors and law enforcement officers who urgently need your help. **

Then the system I served turned on me. False accusations. A political prosecution. My family dragged through absolute hell. The feds even dragged my kids out of our house _in their pajamas._ **But something incredible happened ...** Patriots across this country stood up and helped me fight back.
---
They saved my family. And they reminded me what America is really about. **That 's why my wife Andrea and I built Pipe Hitter Foundation.** So no warrior has to EVER face that fight alone again. **Friend, right now these warriors need help with:** Legal defense costs
• Appeals and court filings
• Emergency family support
• Travel and housing during trials
• Critical evidence investigations But they also need help with the basics: health care, groceries, diapers, everything a family needs to stay afloat. Without support, the system wins. But when patriots step up? _Everything changes._ **You can become part of the network that stands behind these warriors.** You can help them fight back and clear their names. ## Paxton Sues Gerber Over Metals
Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton [announced a lawsuit](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFuhDAQBdDTQGdkDwaWwkUauk2bEo3xAFYMRngC7O0jskdIPZr_9f7Xs3-iD36dPnEhw9cY-5XOFIiZ9n7Di-OafihNtFvaB1qZ9i36HiTUQkmhqh4H9gf1GnNnrHStysmopgVZg6p0PhttXV2OVatVDc0DNNKobQsjPHSjhlLn3txxSqpKKQnQFupRWi3R2UYN1WhdpiU5z3EveCamC9MYXvGgvRjikgczM28pKz8y6DLozvMsvjnhfcygeyPErRBvhrhfBYZAEznB8fKDmAmPl1iIMSThV2HRvsQYo8ugy3fjttOH4FPdZFpOC_rwV83_neww8BsAAP__5KuDVQ) Wednesday against Gerber and its parent company, Nestle USA, accusing them of selling baby food as safe and rigorously tested, even though Gerber's own tests showed dangerous levels of arsenic, lead, and cadmium. Paxton said [67 batches of Gerber rice flour](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO4yAURb8Gd0TwDHEoKLZxN9tuaT3gOUFDTARvYs_frzLRfsHWV_fonvvnY_nAXPJ2_Y138nysddlo74WYqS0PPLhu_Yv6lVqgFmljao-aF1BwllpJbReMnJ-0GBySDyo5PZDXkwN1Bm3NcPOjHR0SUop2CnCJ02qnNTln3IpEcRyyf-G00lZrBeBO-jIGozCFSUe7hiSMopS5thPfiOnAvpbv-qR2ivU-FH9jfnQx_hIwC5j3fT99Pr_oFQqYsXGOhQTMLzMBc6kRi4D5ByRg_qRNvk3lW1Nu1LmQ5HrkKO_EWLoMGL7lWmuS_3pwdlIbM9LotLwggDQQrQyTsZLGiwKdrEYVh-bTY8-l5H6ehFHXO-bys5z_9_Gnh78BAAD__-g_lcU) from 2017 to 2019 contained more than nine times the arsenic level allowed in bottled water. Gerber says its products meet FDA limits and that heavy metals absorbed by crops can't be fully removed. In 2021, an Alaska state lab [found two samples](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LsSnCAYBeCnwQ4HULwUFGnsNm1K5wd-lQTBAdbL22c2-wjpz5w53_n1ml_gvAvrT9hRlXuJc8AreywF03zAXWLIb8wrJo3JYCiYjuhmwURHOaNczmCKO3FuobJKMzvyChXvR8E6wWVbbUoOANg0upXaDoPtlsYawKUZwLKxG2Xl1KeOMy45Z0KMNR8a3TKwuudGLtqSlqF1Jaa6bFjwhrz4J56YahP3yqutlCOT5gcRExHTdV31BXlzYS0x4A27C98oEdMRvTMPEdOG4MtmICERU9t3sh97IqY_GOiXTT9uusPvmKgG_dAlRktN3A8IDjMF73F1YaUWwoopvjP1eKLPNC50QzgfumMBn4mYqqTscTnvXe560rJ1B-f_jS__e_qpxN8AAAD__x3snDA) of Gerber rice cereal over the federal arsenic limit, the suit says. Competitor Beech-Nut recalled its cereal despite lower average readings, while Gerber issued no recall or disclosure. Paxton, the Republican U.S. Senate nominee, is suing under the [Texas Deceptive Trade Practices Act](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuozAQRb8GOkf2YOBRuNiGLttuicZ4AEvGRvaEJH-_IvmE1x8d3XP_3ac7-uDj-hd3Mvxa0hTpWQIxU54OfHGK5UFlpWwpzxSZ8pH8BBI6oaRQ7YQz-5MmjbUzVrpB1WRUP4DsQLW63kwLjW5JAul-abED3fxIPUi00s3Y01x7c-mUVK1SEmC4qZ_GaonO9mpuF-sqLcl5TvnGGzG9sCzhnU7KtzntdTAb81Gq5k8FYwXjB7ApO8r2UXykUi6ughFX8U0SV5P4RgmMTkQqHEhcTrERnm-xE2Mowkdh0b7FkpKrYKyzccfTh-BL11darjv68FnBv33vNPA_AAD__0XCiCQ). The suit says Gerber now posts test results via QR codes on its labels, but its front-of-package safety claims haven't changed.
## Midland Pulls Plug on Flock Cameras
The Midland City Council voted 7-0 Tuesday to [cancel its Flock Safety contract](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uhDAQhJ8GOpB3MX-FizR0lzYlMvZyrGQwMntw9_YReYU0o5FGGs18P4_xYTnw9vy2Kxl5z3Hc6DoCiVAad_uWuB0vOp6UJkqONqG0Rx5RYVOAKqAerRM-adQ292ZSvoecDLQ9qgah1vli0EFjK_TT1M1VrfuZdNdBX3maVUc052zuOlBQAyjEvoSumrSyfmrB1fPkM63Is8RUykJCb3vM4RNPSqWLax7MIrIfWfWV4ZDhcF1X-bFLjHea4XAfynB43WKTsAt025V9sJsvHMuncPG1OQ7FGYWOQiitvFmhAitdKWigLRdZQ56M3y8OgY-mzbR6rpbD3wb5L7vT4G8AAAD__8GzhfA) and have the company haul away the city's 73 license plate reader cameras, just eight months into a two-year deal. In February, Police Chief Greg Snow [credited the cameras](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OqzAQRp_GdCDPhN_CxW3octst0WAPibXGRvYkJG-_yr7C9p--o3O-rsuVfPDx9p92NvLa0hL5LIFFOC8HvSTF8uBy47xythyF85H8ghr7GnQN3UJW_JOXlipnVu0mqNjAMKHuEbq2uhutLU4TDM5OANCO_cgOXM8AulvHzVbefO5AQwegEacGxsvaanLrALbbVqdazc5Lyo3cWfhFZQvv9OTc2LRXwdxFjqIu_xTOCufzPJt3euSVio-fhcL5I6Vw3r0LFF0tnHcfSbjUW0j2uy60sbxrm6JksqJwrrJxx-lD8KUfVKtvO_nwy5O_dnoa_AkAAP__huN_uQ) with recovering 49 stolen vehicles and nearly $4 million in stolen property. name: Josh Shapiro

body:
[ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
Derek, there's a
number from this campaign I'm most proud of, and it might not be what you
expect.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/17548?t=1001&akid=638%2E245147%2EDlnJ9v ]$23.87. That's our average online donation this year.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/17548?t=1002&akid=638%2E245147%2EDlnJ9v ]Twenty-three dollars. Which means tonight's $200,000 fundraising goal
isn’t reached by a handful of people writing big checks — it gets done by
a lot of people giving what they can, when they can. So I'm asking
directly: Will you chip in our average online donation of $23.87 before
midnight and help us crush our last mid-month goal before Election Day?

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/17548?t=1003&akid=638%2E245147%2EDlnJ9v ]Chip in →

Here's why that number matters so much to me,
Derek.

When somebody gives [ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/17548?t=1004&akid=638%2E245147%2EDlnJ9v ]$23.87, they’re deciding that this Commonwealth is
worth a little of their hard-earned money — and I’ll never take that for
granted.

But my opponent? She’s being bankrolled by the National Republican machine
and propped up by Donald Trump (he even attended a fundraiser for her at
Mar-a-Lago!).

Look, I’m not going to pretend $200,000 isn’t a lot of money — because it
is. But this campaign has never been about one person writing one big
check. It’s about the thousands of supporters who have stepped up because
they believe in our vision for Pennsylvania.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/17548?t=1005&akid=638%2E245147%2EDlnJ9v ]So please,
Derek: If you'd rather elect a
Governor who will answer to the good people of Pennsylvania than one who
will answer to far-right insiders and the president, chip in $23.87 or
whatever you can before midnight.

# One Last Thought Until Next Week
---
| | |
---
Hey everybody,
This week, I had hoped to send out some motivating words for the final three weeks of the campaign. Hopefully this motivates you, but it's not how I wanted to do it. Last week, three stories hit the news, and my opponent, Mike Rogers, Chair of the House Armed Services Committee, should have been mentioned repeatedly.
The first was a story about an Iranian attack on a US logistics base in Kuwait. Six US soldiers were killed, and dozens were wounded. The immediate aftermath revealed that the Department of Defense had failed to plan for casualties from Iranian attacks.
Second, Defense Secretary Hegseth announced that Nidal Hasan, who killed thirteen soldiers at Fort Hood, TX, would be publicly executed. In addition to handing our adversaries their greatest propaganda victory in a decade, the execution would be the first public execution in the US in nearly 100 years.
Third, President Trump announced that the US will buy 800,000 metric tons of diesel fuel from Russia in a last-ditch effort to bring down prices before the midterms. Follow this logic: Trump is buying diesel from Russia, which financially supports Iran, to lower high diesel prices that were driven by Trump's war with Iran. Seriously, you really can't make this up.
Each of these stories should have drawn immediate attention from the House Armed Services Committee, and the first two should have led to investigations and inquiries, but you guessed it: Mike Rogers, the committee chair, has said nothing.
Mike has been home since September 18th, when Speaker Johnson closed the House two weeks early to avoid debating a measure to impeach Hegseth. Since then, Rogers has had no public meetings. He has made no public statement. He has simply been incommunicado. If Rogers were in the Armed Forces, he would be charged under Article 92 of the Uniform Code of Military Justice, Dereliction of Duty.
We deserve better leadership in Washington. We deserve accountability. We deserve legislators who want to do their job.
We deserve better.
There are 21 days until the general election. The last day to register to vote is October 19th.
Be well.

We'll talk soon,

Lee

It's unclear whether this will affect Russian attempts to meddle in the midterm elections. | == | | | | == Fierce, bipartisan pushback over Hegseth's plan for livestream execution A bipartisan group of lawmakers is pushing back against Defense Secretary Hegseth's decision to livestream the execution of Nidal Hasan. | == | | | | == House Armed Services Committee Chairman Mike Rogers visits UNC Charlotte to observe defense research in action - Inside UNC Charlotte Mike Rogers (R-Saks) who hasn't had a single meeting in his district in the three weeks the House has been out of session, toured facilities at the University of North Carolina. | == | A CALL TO ACTION | This won't be a year when we can sit back and expect everyone else to do the work. The first was a story about an Iranian attack on a US logistics base in Kuwait. Six US soldiers were killed, and dozens were wounded. Second, Defense Secretary Hegseth announced that Nidal Hasan, who killed thirteen soldiers at Fort Hood, TX, would be publicly executed. If Rogers were in the Armed Forces, he would be charged under Article 92 of the Uniform Code of Military Justice, Dereliction of Duty. We deserve better leadership in Washington. # **[SCOTUS Takes Aim At Sentencing Deference Via Gun Case](https://links.thepricklypear.org/a/2777/click/182/71965/dda07dd487d19bbbbc9b21a13d7da4d82e2381a6/82fdc82aea9eed0b069c5f66e3e89122cac328ac)**

---
The justices heard argument Tuesday in Beaird v. United States, a case asking whether courts must keep deferring to the US Sentencing Commission’s own interpretations of its sentencing guidelines. It is dry on its face and enormous underneath, the next logical step after the Court spent recent terms dismantling the deference regime that let agencies grade their own homework.

---
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the September security incident at RAF Fairford was highly likely coordinated in Iran and almost certainly directed by the IRGC, Britain’s most direct attribution yet of an Iranian operation on its own soil. London sanctioned two Iranians and summoned Tehran’s ambassador. It is the clearest sign that the US war with Iran has already followed the bombers home to allied territory.

The Financial Times reported that the administration warned Kyiv and European capitals it could halt the mechanism Ukraine uses to buy US weapons and cut off intelligence-sharing, to pressure Ukraine into stopping its deep strikes on Russian oil refineries. A US official denied making any explicit threat, and nothing has actually been cut, but the report lays bare the fault line running through the Republican coalition on Ukraine.

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Let me explain my decision, Derek:
body:
The work that will decide the midterms — and whether or not we can put a stop to Trump — is happening right now, and the DNC is spearheading that effort. [](https://ak.democrats.org/go/89216?t=1&akid=9888%2E22930333%2Eugp7sA)
---
Derek, this is an email from the Democratic National Committee about our work to flip Congress in 19 days. If you'd like to stop receiving emails about this contest, please [click here.](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/warren-sweepstakes-2026-opt-out/?t=2&akid=9888%2E22930333%2Eugp7sA) | [](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-warren-sweepstakes-2026?amount=7&refcode=em_20261015_9888_fr&refcode2=9888_22930333_ugp7sA&akid=9888%2E22930333%2Eugp7sA)
---
**Derek, will you meet me in Boston or DC?**
I’m traveling the country mobilizing voters and campaigning for fighters in battleground races, and my favorite part is meeting Democrats on the ground. That’s why, if you [**chip in $7, or any amount, to the DNC today,**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-warren-sweepstakes-2026?refcode=em_20261015_9888_fr&amount=7&refcode2=9888_22930333_ugp7sA&akid=9888%2E22930333%2Eugp7sA) you’ll be entered to win a trip, travel, and hotel included, to meet me in Boston or DC.
**[ENTER TO WIN](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-warren-sweepstakes-2026?refcode=em_20261015_9888_fr&amount=7&refcode2=9888_22930333_ugp7sA&akid=9888%2E22930333%2Eugp7sA)**
Let me explain my decision: The DNC is the _only_ organization that works year-round, every year, to elect Democrats at every level. From the school board to the presidency, _every_ Democrat running for office relies on resources that the DNC provides.
**The work that will decide the midterms — and whether or not we can put a stop to Trump — is happening right now, and the DNC is spearheading that effort.** They’ve kick-started a **first-of-its-kind partisan voter registration program** in battleground districts, working to register thousands of new Democratic voters. They’ve hosted their **largest-ever training for campaign staff** , and they are working to **build a team of voter protection volunteers** that can stand up to any threats to election integrity the Trump administration may throw our way.
**Derek,_all_ of those things are only possible because of grassroots supporters like you.** Over 99% of the DNC’s contributions come from texts, ads, letters, and emails just like this one asking regular people for their support.
_That_ is why I want the opportunity to thank one of you in person. Grassroots supporters are the lifeblood of the Democratic Party, and if we take back our majorities this November, _your_ support will be the reason why.
[**So, Derek, will you chip in $7, or any amount, for a chance to meet? I would love to meet you.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-warren-sweepstakes-2026?refcode=em_20261015_9888_fr&amount=7&refcode2=9888_22930333_ugp7sA&akid=9888%2E22930333%2Eugp7sA)

name: Chris Pappas
subject: What happened in our first debate
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
What he won’t say on stage vs. what he says behind closed doors
# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=9546%2E582294%2EzMZh92)
It’s Chris.
At our first debate on Tuesday, the moderator asked John Sununu a simple question: What is your specific proposal for saving Social Security? Here’s what he said:
[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261015_2.Azx5fY&refcode=em20261015-2&t=2&akid=9546%2E582294%2EzMZh92)
He won’t say what his plan is because he knows how deeply unpopular it is. But Granite Staters know the truth: **John Sununu was a leading architect of the scheme to privatize Social Security.** Then at an AARP forum with Granite Staters, he would only say his old plan doesn’t fit today’s needs.
My answer is simple. People pay into Social Security their whole working lives, and they deserve to know it’ll be there when they retire. **I’ll oppose any cuts to benefits, and I won’t tell anyone they have to work longer to get what they’ve already earned.**
That wasn’t the only question Sununu dodged. When he was asked whether he would have voted to confirm Pete Hegseth, RFK Jr., and Kristi Noem, he said:
**_“I wouldn’t have voted for all three of those, and I’m not going to litigate each one of them.”_**
So he would have confirmed at least some of them, and he won’t tell you which ones. **Hegseth was confirmed by a single tie-breaking vote.** In the Senate one vote can decide who runs the Pentagon. Now the so-called Secretary of War almost livestreamed an execution. That madness could have been stopped by one Senator. But Sununu won’t tell us whether or not it would have been him.
This is the same John Sununu who cheered on Trump’s war in Iran, calling it a success. That war has sent New Hampshire’s energy prices to record highs. I’ve voted to end it, and I’ll keep fighting to rein it in.
And behind closed doors, John Sununu was caught on camera saying the quiet part out loud. **_He said this race “is important to President Trump’s agenda and to the successes that have been made in Washington.”_**
That’s who he’d be working for. **He has Donald Trump’s endorsement and tens of millions of dollars in outside Republican money behind him.** With 19 days until Election Day, they’re betting New Hampshire voters won’t notice what he refuses to say in public.
**We’re going to make sure they do. But I need your help to keep our message on the air.**
**[Will you chip in $5 right now to help us hold John Sununu accountable and win this seat?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261015_2.Azx5fY&refcode=em20261015-2&t=3&akid=9546%2E582294%2EzMZh92)**

Thank you for being in this with me,
Chris
**New Hampshire is poised to be one of the closest Senate races in the country. Will you chip in today to help Chris stop the Republicans from flipping the Granite State red and expanding their Senate majority?**
**[Donate »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_cp_footer?refcode=em20261015-2&t=23&refcode2=9546_582294_zMZh92&akid=9546%2E582294%2EzMZh92)**

name: Barack Obama
subject: Peter, if you’re reading this, you’re not like most Democrats
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the National Democratic Redistricting Committee, John Bisognano, President
body:
Not everyone is paying attention to state-level races. You’re different, Peter

---
Peter, it’s Barack. More people should be paying attention to the key state-level elections on the ballot this November. Because with so much at stake, _it's hard to overstate the importance of these races to the future of our country_. That’s because leaders at the state level oversee elections. They draw the maps for Congress and state legislatures. They make decisions that ultimately make it easier (or harder) to vote. And with free and fair elections under attack — from mid-decade gerrymandering and threats of voter suppression — we need more state-level officials who care about building a stronger democracy. The National Democratic Redistricting Committee, which I co-founded with Attorney General Eric Holder, fights alongside its affiliates to elect state lawmakers and governors who are on the side of the people — who believe in fair maps and fair access to the ballot. The NDRC also fights to elect fair-minded judges who won’t bend the law or twist the rules of our democracy to help out a political party. **[The NDRC needs your help. They’ve endorsed over 300 Democracy Defenders who are up for election in 19 days in over a dozen states across the country. And they need more grassroots donations to help get leaders like them over the finish line so they can fight for fair maps across the country. More people should be paying attention to the key state-level elections on the ballot this November. Because with so much at stake, it's hard to overstate the importance of these races to the future of our country. That’s because leaders at the state level oversee elections. They draw the maps for Congress and state legislatures. They make decisions that ultimately make it easier (or harder) to vote. And with free and fair elections under attack — from mid-decade gerrymandering and threats of voter suppression — we need more state-level officials who care about building a stronger democracy. Social Security benefits will [rise 3.6% next year](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwyAQBuCnwZstOINtBoYu3tK1IyJwJFcREwG1lbev3KpP0O2kk_5f3_9xsRdHibbbu3ugaTHbDY-asDUstmZPLlX0X4XaqziqmFPA2ixwmHrBe6Gs8412tNJ1wUREwLFDI2YNfJqkEt3dAA8qRhx5iEouctbLddFuDo57fUU1dmTOPMGFEiAk10MUEkGIBZT3ELVikmOglsvwmWlrd4zplXcsg8-PLpl7a8_KxjcGK4P1OI7BX-vpOP8M1vNksP5y-j9P73NyPXCYe9p8QVeRwdoVE54HpUR1mpnkt4ej9NPT_jnPbuA7AAD__zalerI), the biggest cost-of-living bump since 2023. For the average retiree, that works out to about $75 more a month, lifting the typical check to roughly $2,170 starting in January. The adjustment affects [76 million Americans](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOqzAQheGnMV2QZzAmFC5uQ5fbbokcMw6zMjiyZ0F5-1W22BfY9hS_9J2P23zznHh__PcbOYl53umsiUSozDUH9qlS-Cosr-K5Uk4LVZlRo72AvkA_-yB80Gx8s7hIhNQ15GAYUVtremhWN3Z-6Oz1bkzQGK_2HijAANRDtxi0XcPu3QMNPSAYPbYRDCHAFfsQMI69MpoWllzaz8y7rBTTKx9U2pC3JrlV5FlV90_hpHA6z7Ot1bePfCic3hyFE-0KJ78cOXih9_ArMO0qW2qKW54np8TVDsrox-Y5_eTlj68cDr8DAAD__4hRdQs), including 7.3 million on Supplemental Security Income, whose higher payments arrive Dec. 31. Personalized COLA notices go out by mail in December or online in late November for anyone with a My Social Security account. Those who want the paperless version must opt in by Nov. 18. ## Oldest Known Shipwreck Found Off Turkey
Archaeologists have found what they believe is the world's oldest shipwreck, a [Bronze Age trade vessel](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuozAQRb8GOkczgyGhcLFNumy7JXLscZiNg5HtBPH3T7z3Ca-8utLR0fl3m25WoiyPv_bFpoY0LbyVyLVynkpyYmNh985S92ylcIqeS50IaFAICvvJuiofnrRtvQnMxF3LBs8jwTDoHtvZXOAO7DUyO22d5g7cpQPqg2ccw8itmIOHgD0SahhPATUT4oV65yiMfaOBvdSUT_-TLHXmEPf04Xxy6dVGM9e6lqb709C1oevKaY18XA1dt5SjL-pHW5VZ1i2zeypvqywPdbfuqbQGUDvbrLwUd3DZq-XY9Z2fvCskPHdAY5uNXzeJUcpwbjQ8Xlbit0P9ZbqPoa8AAAD__5sAhOs) that sank off Turkey's Mediterranean coast between 4,400 and 4,700 years ago, around the time the Great Pyramid was going up. The wooden hull is long gone, but more than 30 ceramic jars and three stone anchors still sit on an underwater slope about 98 feet down near Kekova Island in Antalya. Researchers think the 33-foot ship was hauling cargo along the coast, possibly bound for Troy or Crete. [Watch a video here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u3CAQhZ8Gd1gwxj8UFGnc3bQpLRaG68liswLW1r59RPIIaaY6mvN959fX9mUp0vn90x5oakjbiXeJWCvmrSRHNhZ070z1ky0VTNFjqRsImLgUXI6bdZUu3JTtvAmIgEOHRs4axDSpUXa7wVHPIB9op0lrtbhHcAh6ljboZVgeQ0em_ZNCjhKkEroPUiFIucDoHAQ9MiXQU025_53orDuG-EkX5t6lo4tmr_VV2PCDwcpgve-7x3dOTaQFGKwXeUwM1lbDYJWiHdWyKUdf-D8rXnZ63Rndk3sqrhWg5ykEXt_5iZ_Cj0aBOdsT7cldsqV22fjXTTFSmWamxPdhKf7lqv8552XgTwAAAP__Yj-L_g). Several jars still hold hardened black residue, which could be olive oil, wine, or tree resin. Clay analysis suggests the jars were made in [workshops in the Jordan Valley](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2y2yAURlcjdWjgCrApKNK4c9qUGgwXixgJD1xZo91nlPd28Poz5_v5c5_uLuW0Pn-7BS3FMq24t4xEWKdWfHK5od9qoqO61LDkgI0m4KCZ4EyoyXlKH5yk64ONiIBjj1ZcDHCtpRL9bLUBES4AUoz68bh6cH58RGOuSirjjOqTPX2CCyVASG6GKCSCEFdQ3kM0qpMcQ6JSh78lrTRjzEf5YB18WfpsZ6J368ZfHdw6uO37PtBWX-lAKsEdJ9TBzW-ZtoonUGoOjX1NYW1O772if7Ft9acUAysxsm9FY8sZjbW6Fd3KfHGN2AgjB236asN7Tzmnpi-d5M_Fpfy_FP3wy4-FfwEAAP__w4OMPg). One jar appears to have been used to churn butter, suggesting the crew kept goats on board for milk. The find beats the previous record holder, a wreck off the Greek island of Dokos, by [a few centuries](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2y2yAQhZ8GdWhgDfiqoEij7qZNqcGwWMQIPLCyRm-fUfIIabba8_OdX9_Lt0s5ledPt6GlWJeCR89IhG3p1SeXO_q9JTqbSx1rDthpAQGGS8GlXpyn9MFFuSHYiAh4G9DK-wTCGKXlsNpJ3Cac8GFU8Fp_3aN2DzBRGghRmCkOyV5-UkgtQSoxjVEqBCm_QHsPcdJMCQyJaht_11RoxZjP-sE2-roN2a5E785uPxjMDObjOEZasThKtbh88Vx_DGbXqHO_Z9obMpivUAazFNdRl7K2HDr_x8hfpR6F9zW9j4b-xXPtxLfakNPqCldCCH6ia527Z-Wx7iXwGiOnvb3wZDAPzYb3kXJO3dyZEs_Npfy3Mv3n0h8LfwIAAP__YvuUmw). The artifacts will go on display at a new underwater archaeology museum in Antalya opening in the coming months.

subject: MAGA Republicans thought they could draw us out!
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY FRIENDS OF GLORIA JOHNSON, LISA SORENSEN, TREASURER
body:
As you've likely noticed, this election season isn't quite going as they'd planned...

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/0a28850ac720/stand-up-against-the-shameful-gop-power-grab-7363938?e=dc5f639d62)
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
|
---
| |

Friends,
MAGA Republicans tried their hardest to divide us. They redrew our congressional maps in May - a power grab without precedent in our state's history. They thought they could demoralize Democrats, carve good candidates out of their districts, and cling to power. But as you've likely noticed, this election season isn't quite going as they'd planned...
From Memphis to Knoxville and in between, progressive Democratic candidates are undeterred. They're outraising their Republican opponents, they're running strong campaigns, and they're poised to shock the country in November.
Take my friend, State Rep. Justin Pearson. Recent polling shows Justin is [within striking distance](https://us.list-manage.com/k4fzAHDobI0?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0) of an upset victory in Tennessee's 9th congressional district. Just last week, the national Democratic Party moved Justin's campaign to its ["Red to Blue" list](https://us.list-manage.com/EAie1NRd1Kt?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0). This is yet another sign that Justin is running a campaign that can actually win, and Democrats and Republicans alike are taking notice.
Days after that news, [Time magazine](https://us.list-manage.com/pgtf4UfLuRy?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0) profiled Justin's candidacy, where my friend said it best:
_“This is just another challenge that we are going to face, and we're going to face it together. And we're going to show up more than we have in decades. We're going to participate more than we have in decades because our voting rights are on the ballot.”_
As Early Vote is beginning, it's time for all of us who care about the future of our state and country to stand strong with these Democratic candidates. Organizations like [TN Rise PAC](https://us.list-manage.com/1CgkuraHqGO?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0) are doing vital work to bolster Democratic candidates like Justin who are best-positioned to win in competitive races. Polling shows that these candidates can win, but only if enough voters hear their message and turn out to vote. I support the work that TN Rise PAC does and they can use your support. [Learn how you can support the work of TN Rise PAC](https://us.list-manage.com/JmfcGlO0XP5?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0).

Thank you, and let's go win this!
Gloria

Yes, I know we email about a lot of deadlines. But this one is particularly important.
Trump has pledged up to $500 million to hold the Senate, and Republican groups have already put $743 million into the 13 most competitive Senate races, more than double the $309 million Democrats have put in. They're outspending us in nine of them.

name: Beto O'Rourke
subject: I want to tell you about my friend Joe Kennedy and the work he’s doing with Groundwork PAC.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Powered by People, [poweredxpeople
body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=241122%2E444211%2EE8nh2T)
For as long as I’ve been doing this work, a lot of “smart” people have told me it’s a waste of time. “Texas is too big, too expensive, young people don’t vote.”
I’ve heard the same thing said about Mississippi, Oklahoma, North Dakota, and plenty of other places that the establishment decided a long time ago weren’t worth the trouble.
That’s why I want to tell you about my friend Joe Kennedy and the work he’s doing with Groundwork PAC.
Joe started Groundwork because he got tired of watching our party invest in the same handful of places every cycle while expecting a different result. Groundwork backs the candidates in red states that others gave up on.
It’s the same reason we built Powered by People here in Texas. Our volunteers get trained, then head out to campuses, coffee shops, and concerts, meeting people where they are and staying in touch with every one of them until they vote. And it works. In 2024, young voters in our program turned out at 79%. The statewide average was 39%.
I don’t believe there’s any such thing as a throwaway state, or a community whose voice matters less because of where they live. Neither does Joe.
Early voting in Texas is starting in just 4 days and people are already starting to vote in states across the country.
[**That’s why I’m asking: Will you split a $3 donation between Groundwork PAC and Powered by People today to help us both reach voters and elect Democrats up and down the ballot in places overlooked by the establishment?**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20261015-1.SUz05a&refcode=ema20261015-241122&t=3&akid=241122%2E444211%2EE8nh2T)

Grassroots Update

THURSDAY, OCTOBER 15, 2026

HI EVERYONE,

Fantastic work on the call banking. We have finished calls into the mail in precincts and now we move on to the remaining
outstanding absentee ballots. The script is still the same, but you'll see a new call list available to you. Your calls are making
a difference! Over the past few days, we have seen a large number of our called voters return their ballots. Those are votes for
our candidates. Keep it up!

volunteers to gather and work together. We are looking to grow our volunteer team and add more office volunteers. Please click the
