Today marks one year since I launched my campaign for governor of Texas, and looking back on how far we've come, I couldn't be more grateful to have y'all by my side.
Thanks to you, six polls in the last month have me leading Greg Abbott. We've raised over $25 million to connect with voters and get our message out. And with your support, 19 days from now I will be the next Governor of Texas.
I've driven all across Texas and everyone is saying the same thing: they want Greg Abbott out of the Governor's mansion and a government that works for them. Because there is no town he won't sell out and no Texan he won't leave behind.
This election is our chance to undo all the damage Greg Abbott has caused.
**Together, we have to fight for the future of Texas. My plan is simple: secure the American Dream by saving our public schools and putting money back in your pocket.**_**Not raise property taxes. And definitely not create an income tax.**_

body:
Authoritarianism binds the nation through fear. Democracy binds it through faith.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=4000%2E21716%2EbdJTEc)
With just a few weeks left until the midterms, I know there’s a lot of vitriol online right now. If you’re feeling frustrated, it’s important to remember that a pretty significant amount of that hate isn’t even coming from real people — **it’s coming from bots.**
The sad truth is that authoritarians around the world have realized that they can erode the faith and functionality of democracy through a mirage of division that stokes real division.
This dynamic is often whispered about in the corridors of power throughout the transatlantic alliance, but too often leaders have been wary to emphasize it for fear of sounding conspiratorial.
Thankfully, that’s changing. In recent months, it’s become apparent to _everyone_ just how many bots are flooding our social media feeds with hate and division. And we shouldn’t shy away from it for fear of Trump mocking it as a “Russian hoax” while he both benefits from the bot farms and rewards Putin with more money to fight Ukraine.
**We need to speak clearly on this threat and get a handle on it.** Any Big Tech regulation by the US, UK, and EU must grapple with foreign interference through social media. And I’m going to keep speaking up about it until we take real action.
Above all, we have to remember that authoritarianism binds the nation through fear. But democracy binds the nation through faith: faith in your neighbors’ better angels, and faith in your own capacity to tap into them.
**If you’re with me, I need your help. Sarah McBride

Hi Peter,

As election day nears, James Talarico is letting his "moderate" mask slip.

When asked at a recent campaign event who his favorite drag queen was, he didn't miss a beat - instantly rattling "their" name off like he'd been asked his favorite color.

That video has gone viral online, racking up millions of views on social media.

Talarico has spent this entire campaign trying to sell Texas voters on a moderate, Bible-quoting version of himself, and videos like this are the LAST thing Talarico's campaign wants getting out to Texas voters.

Texas voters outside Austin won't buy his facade, not once they see the real Talarico instead of the campaign-trail version.

And right now in Michigan, Democrat U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed is running the same playbook, holding town halls in Lansing, Grand Rapids, Detroit, Flint, and Macomb, hoping moderate suburban voters forget he wants abortion legal through all nine months.

My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I'm the President of Students for Life Action. You can think of us as the grassroots arm of the Pro-Life Movement.

Peter, here's my problem.

You and I can't rely on the national media to tell the truth about these politicians' abortion extremism.

So it's up to grassroots folks like you and me to hold them accountable.
That's exactly what I want to do with my rapid response counter-protests at as many candidate events as possible in our targeted races.

[Will you please chip in right now to keep our rapid response team ready to move the moment we get word of the next public event](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=79f9afbdaefa4742aee4660df1f184ce&_e=yeyehx4_Uk43IYdbfVOBnprRVjoEaedTc_iqP24fs-eMarrhrDDdTZdSebuzmSzg_mnV1UTNwqj64albPWQ0PbAkR_CRouFa5Ol0Z5idmws3ReBLGR3JAQav2Lnwt1CQV2TBwD67XvbICEhFjxDDzD7puwMpSIAP5GHujK00-qzMcy9LFBRP7dK3EtOz1-F3QdEhKIjD8FjK7mZ7H-lF5R0FRRSsVXk2qwjVcxZ4aVEFQsNzemDb-rTwDOqKaHew9aQEhUyC67Zwigq0WOLDfV9JLC19ksGTBcdH4WRM6TcoNVxp7eZJmSq5MVH_nARCgu5cQ_sbD930OgzdZCWNXnukL29fkHKsJfBHVl_O8Zg9tVAGgT7RiZz6adUlst5_Pm-jbWUNhuGmqAJV2hVSXhYwXU5jRPf-clewvGk_clMhz-LhmpdYvif2YEQoOxujvq9elb9vERNHZ9mDM6y13hYYP63vd2RFVSS1uYR6vdofkJTrnjv3Lpua3zYJmlVMlGEQFUg6YijlrhCDhNKP_z7dKX2Aiynza2qM9uM7ffa0xxQFOBEJKwZFlCw6n0mQ6YogaIBzo68_iEhTP8Kgt5PF_hcEtrZL6ppntmKidzsfb4tD5mSGJCGmHPq0J8hLJJtx0Abm1ocHPtdeG3QeKw%3D%3D)**?**

Last month, our Pro-Life Generation activists launched the first stop of a 100-church flyering campaign at a church right in Talarico's back yard.

Then, when he spoke at Baylor University - a Baptist school - our team was on the ground to ensure attendees heard the truth about his anti-Biblical, pro-abortion stance.

Do you remember, back in 2024, when our students walked into a Kamala Harris rally in Wisconsin, held up a cross, and got mocked from the stage for it?

A video went viral of Kamala on stage, talking about abortion "rights" and overturning Roe v. Wade, denouncing Christians who said "Christ is King," and responding to our students with "You guys are at the wrong rally."

I've seen it time and time again.

These are exactly the moments on the campaign trail that can swing an entire election.

One month from today, on Tuesday, November 3rd, voters across the nation will decide who controls Congress for the next two years - and who has the momentum heading into the critical 2028 presidential cycle.

Talarico, El-Sayed, and all pro-abortion politicians know a camera catching them off-script is worth more than any ad buy. That's exactly why they're not publishing their schedules more than a day or two out.

So my team has to be ready before they announce, not after.

That means canvassers who can redirect on short notice and students who'll show up with signs and cameras of their own.

None of that comes free, and none of it waits for a fundraising deadline.

[Peter, will you please make your most generous contribution to keep Students for Life Action ready to move the second one of these campaigns tips their hand](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=79f9afbdaefa4742aee4660df1f184ce&_e=yeyehx4_Uk43IYdbfVOBnprRVjoEaedTc_iqP24fs-eMarrhrDDdTZdSebuzmSzg_mnV1UTNwqj64albPWQ0PbAkR_CRouFa5Ol0Z5idmws3ReBLGR3JAQav2Lnwt1CQV2TBwD67XvbICEhFjxDDzD7puwMpSIAP5GHujK00-qzcfNTQhDURIzYcX24byVlH25TtEAYHPrOhzAIHCyKggyEPfxeyK6MeW6tIqnwlmHc8A9O1CHMC9Y24JL_ctJcTNVEU9yhq15LFRIA2c1-mDFUjBB0npDJU81pRR7ZVDOYKr8Vz-aw7G7nUda1KpGG_S8g6NV6zCSbVR1fEhF1HICrTfNlDYnuIZax68cLgPYKvM0da73bGoQgDvFA1TfC3YUVHR3MAvUBhq7IzyxXIkIXlrfucleoDZDANxteEBeLelVdCWO5mUIPlyAEiKyvbodldcJXFBPepOkZI-o7r3T0QZ8ZYlZKLAORFPOxGeY8S42hR08WR6_fjL1x_MvmAX_hROFvoVO5D63bo1bDxkbzb5NVL5XRkQiPLB9Bv_DK7j9nAOexojhAwwAzaxm2lTOXWcD0m0P19a67_3LblMq1pV357GdCQHbSbJpKDK5ZjxuEZtQ-uZwHFNLxqetBhZ2US3WBA9onj0EMZcV9ESA%3D%3D)**?**

clean_body: Hi Peter, As election day nears, James Talarico is letting his "moderate" mask slip. When asked at a recent campaign event who his favorite drag queen was, he didn't miss a beat - instantly rattling "their" name off like he'd been asked his favorite color. That video has gone viral online, racking up millions of views on social media. Talarico has spent this entire campaign trying to sell Texas voters on a moderate, Bible-quoting version of himself, and videos like this are the LAST thing Talarico's campaign wants getting out to Texas voters. Texas voters outside Austin won't buy his facade, not once they see the real Talarico instead of the campaign-trail version. And right now in Michigan, Democrat U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed is running the same playbook, holding town halls in Lansing, Grand Rapids, Detroit, Flint, and Macomb, hoping moderate suburban voters forget he wants abortion legal through all nine months. My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I'm the President of Students for Life Action. You can think of us as the grassroots arm of the Pro-Life Movement. Peter, here's my problem. You and I can't rely on the national media to tell the truth about these politicians' abortion extremism. So it's up to grassroots folks like you and me to hold them accountable. That's exactly what I want to do with my rapid response counter-protests at as many candidate events as possible in our targeted races. ? Last month, our Pro-Life Generation activists launched the first stop of a 100-church flyering campaign at a church right in Talarico's back yard. Then, when he spoke at Baylor University - a Baptist school - our team was on the ground to ensure attendees heard the truth about his anti-Biblical, pro-abortion stance. Do you remember, back in 2024, when our students walked into a Kamala Harris rally in Wisconsin, held up a cross, and got mocked from the stage for it? A video went viral of Kamala on stage, talking about abortion "rights" and overturning Roe v. Wade, denouncing Christians who said "Christ is King," and responding to our students with "You guys are at the wrong rally." I've seen it time and time again. These are exactly the moments on the campaign trail that can swing an entire election. One month from today, on Tuesday, November 3rd, voters across the nation will decide who controls Congress for the next two years - and who has the momentum heading into the critical 2028 presidential cycle. Talarico, El-Sayed, and all pro-abortion politicians know a camera catching them off-script is worth more than any ad buy. That's exactly why they're not publishing their schedules more than a day or two out. So my team has to be ready before they announce, not after. That means canvassers who can redirect on short notice and students who'll show up with signs and cameras of their own. None of that comes free, and none of it waits for a fundraising deadline. ? Have you seen the latest news about Elon Musk?
Elon Musk has spent over $276 million this cycle to help Republicans — and a big chunk of that went toward the **Republican Governors Association (RGA).**
The RGA exists solely to keep MAGA governors in power. And right now, MAGA Gov. Joe Lombardo is one of the governors they’re fighting hardest to protect.
Well, I’ve got news for Elon Musk: **Nevada isn’t for sale.**
I’ve never backed down from folks with more money and more power than me, and I’m not about to start now. Musk can spend all he wants, but he can’t knock on doors in Henderson. He can’t talk to his neighbors in Reno. He can’t show up for Nevada families the way we can.
We can out-organize this money, but that takes a lot of resources — and with three weeks to go, every dollar counts.
**[Please, chip in $5 or whatever you can afford to help us beat Elon’s money and flip Nevada blue. Hi, friend,

From the start of this campaign, I have thought about why I made the decision to run for the U.S. Senate in Kansas.

I’m a husband, a father of two remarkable daughters and a grandfather. I’m also the founding pastor of the largest United Methodist Church in the United States and a proud fifth-generation Kansan.

My great-great grandparents moved to Dickinson County, Kansas, 147 years ago. They were farmers and builders and good people who helped build their communities of Hope and Elmo. Like them, I love Kansas and its people and I love my country. **That’s why I feel called to run for the U.S. Senate.**
Today, our nation’s highest values and aspirations are being undermined, and chaos and corruption in Washington are tearing Americans apart. We’ve insulted and alienated our allies. And we have a government in D.C. that’s making life harder for Kansans. People can’t afford the basics — food, gas and healthcare.
[**_I’m running for the U.S. Senate because I care about our country, because things need to change, and because I know I can build bridges, bring people together to solve problems and be a champion for Kansas._**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141502105/653764161/-540544497?amounts=10,25,50,100,250&refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk784&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjYxMjYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOTgyMzQxYjUtZDNjOC1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNGZiZTgzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=5uNt0Erkv1I8dsKxhduiF03xgruvVvZ7qS2FD7NGvvk=)
I’ve heard from Kansans all over the state who voted for Roger Marshall six years ago and now feel he’s not listening to them — people who have met with him and often feel unseen or dismissed by the man they elected to represent them.

And now, this race has gotten close. Between political experts and polls, it’s clear we have a real chance to win here in Kansas and get to work for families.

I believe we can and must do more — and as the leader of a large, diverse congregation of roughly equal parts Democrats, Republicans and independents, I am ready to disrupt partisan gridlock in Washington, bring people together and create meaningful solutions to our problems.
[**_That work starts _now_ , and if you agree that what’s going on in our country is unacceptable, then I need you with me. Nothing about this race will be easy, and we’re going to need an incredible grassroots team to create change in Kansas. Please consider joining us now by making a grassroots donation._**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141502106/653764162/-540544497?amounts=10,25,50,100,250&refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk784&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjYxMjYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOTgyMzQxYjUtZDNjOC1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNGZiZTgzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=5uNt0Erkv1I8dsKxhduiF03xgruvVvZ7qS2FD7NGvvk=)

2. **Not enough politicians were fighting for families like mine** —the ones clipping coupons, driving minivans, and worrying about rising costs.

I ran to change that—by _relentlessly_ focusing on making government work for everyday families, and by never selling out my values for a corporate check.

Katie Porter

clean_body: | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Friend, I was a 26-year-old law student out for a run when a tree fell on me. It shattered my spine and in an instant, I lost my ability to ever walk again. I won't pretend that my journey in a wheelchair has been easy, but what I can tell you is that every time someone tells me what I can't do, I think about that morning in 1984. As an attorney, as a Texas Supreme Court Justice, as Attorney General, and now as Governor - the same lesson that got me through my accident has never failed me: No challenge is too great to overcome if you put in the work, refuse to give up, and lean on your faith and the people who love you. "That’s all I’m asking you to do today. Get to work. Give what you can. Let’s make sure the Texas we love is still here for our children and our grandchildren." | I am proud of what we have built together in Texas: the strongest economy in America, the best state to do business, and a beacon of freedom and opportunity for all. But I have never been more aware that these things can be taken away. This cycle, the Democrats have a plan. They have national money flooding in. They have their biggest names in Texas, firing up their base, trying to flip seats they never could have dreamed of flipping just four years ago. But I've got a plan, too. Friends,

With under three weeks until Election Day, **so much is at stake, from the future of our democracy to the values that define us as a country. But this election is about more than what we are fighting against—it’s also about what we are fighting for!** I grew up in a blue-collar family right here in the Hudson Valley, believing that if you work hard, you can get ahead. **I am running to make that belief a reality once more by tackling the affordability crisis affecting so many families here at home.** **Making homeownership possible** Our police officers, nurses, teachers, and first responders should be able to afford a home in the communities they serve. But right now, coming up with a 20% down payment is simply out of reach for most people. In Congress, I will create America’s first Public Service Home Loan Program to give these community heroes access to competitive mortgage interest rates, with no down payment and no private mortgage insurance payments. **Making healthcare affordable** Growing up, my dad worked construction. His ability to earn a living depended on staying healthy, but he couldn’t always afford health insurance. No family should face that reality. In Congress, I will fight to extend the expanded ACA tax credits and establish a public option that lets people buy into Medicare at any age, increasing competition while preserving choice. **Lowering everyday costs** Lowering the cost of everyday life means ending Trump’s reckless tariffs, which are costing Hudson Valley households $4,200 a year. It also means holding monopoly utility companies accountable by cracking down on unjustified rate hikes and making sure working families aren’t left footing the bill for corporate profits. **Hard work should be enough to get ahead in the Hudson Valley. In Congress, I’ll fight every day to make sure it is.** With gratitude and fire, Cait Conley

Ahmed Al-Issai, in his 60s, has resorted to living in the courtyard of Al-Thawrah Hospital in Taiz city, Yemen. October 15, 2026. Photo by Khalid Al-Banna.
TAIZ, Yemen--Like other residents of Taiz, Hael Mohammed is struggling to find food and other life essentials for his family as an escalating war between Ansarallah and a Saudi-led coalition draws in on the city.
"No one can imagine how difficult the journey is just to find a propane cylinder or a bag of wheat in this city," the 41-year-old pharmacist and father of three told Drop Site News. "Many food traders told me their stores have run out of wheat, rice, and other essentials. When I finally found wheat, it was nearly double its normal price."
Mohammed said that residents across Taiz are stockpiling food, fearing they could be trapped in their homes as the ground battles close in. The third largest city in Yemen, located in the southwestern highlands, Taiz has long been on the front line of Yemen's civil war--and is now encircled by fighting.
Taiz governorate consists of 23 districts, 20 of which are now under Ansarallah control. Only three districts remain under control by the internationally recognized government--the three that comprise Taiz city itself.
Ansarallah now controls all entry points to Taiz city. These entrances have turned into active frontlines with only brief pauses in fighting. Drivers are forced to wait for the short lulls--which usually last no more than a few hours a day--to enter or leave the city.
The continuous fighting has sparked widespread terror among residents, who fear the conflict could reach their homes at any moment. The road blockades have also had severe economic consequences: fuel and basic commodities can no longer enter regularly, driving prices up to three times their normal cost for essential items like fuel.
While some food trucks have managed to enter the city in recent weeks, supply has fallen far short of demand, with residents scrambling to stock up on supplies as the fighting rages on the outskirts.
"The fighting is less than five kilometers (about 3 miles) from my home, and that is reason enough for me to be worried. I successfully purchased a 25-kilogram bag of wheat flour and I have cooking gas," Mohammed said. But he has been forced to go into debt to afford food. "That was the only way to secure food for my family," Mohammed said. "I went into debt even though I have a salary, so what about those who are unemployed or displaced? It must be much worse for them."
For now he is buying bread from a local bakery, even though it costs 50% more than usual, preferring to preserve his cooking gas and flour rather than face another desperate search for supplies later on. "We won't use the gas until we are completely unable to leave our home," he said.
## **A Growing Humanitarian Crisis**
Last month, Ansarallah (also known as the Houthis) swept south from their northern stronghold in a lightning offensive, launching heavy attacks on Saudi-backed government forces in southern Hodeidah and western Taiz governorate. The Houthis quickly took control of the strategic city of Mocha and Yemen's Red Sea coast to control the Bab al-Mandab strait, a vital waterway for global shipping.
At the beginning of October, Ansarallah launched another major offensive against government forces in southern and western Taiz governorate. By October 4, they had made significant advances, seizing the main road linking Taiz city to the governorate's southern and western areas, as well as to Lahj governorate.
The United Nations World Food Program (WFP) warned on Wednesday the fighting and road closures have cut off humanitarian assistance to some 800,000 people in Taiz and other affected areas. Wheat flour stocks are nearly exhausted, while remaining food supplies in local markets may last only a short time.
In May, even before the latest phase of fighting, the UN warned that more than 22 million people required humanitarian assistance and protection services across Yemen, including 5.2 million who were displaced. The recent escalation in the military conflict has forced an additional 201,217 people from their homes, according to data released last week by the International Organization for Migration. The number is continuing to rise every day.
Streets in Taiz city that used to be crowded late into the night are now largely deserted. As a result of the road closures into the city, the price of fuel has nearly tripled, with 20 liters (5.3 gallons) of petrol rising from 30,000 Yemeni riyals (around $19) to 90,000 riyals (around $57). Few cars and buses move through the streets by day, and almost none at night due to the security risks.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2001d972-46b6-4261-8e76-3f61f107ca33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The normally bustling 26 September street in Taiz city is largely empty as residents stay indoors amid growing security concerns and a fuel crisis. October 2026. Photo by Khalid Al-Banna.
Aside from the huge rise in transportation costs, getting food and other goods into the city has become a harrowing ordeal.
"All the breadwinners went to the market at once to buy food, so it is only natural that our stores ran out," a food trader told Drop Site News. He agreed to speak on the condition of anonymity for security concerns. Several food traders declined to be interviewed about the crisis, fearing accusations of price gouging and hoarding from local residents. "There are drivers who wait sometimes for days for the fighting to pause--even if for just a few minutes or an hour--so they can enter the city with wheat, rice, or other supplies."
The food trader said that deliveries take significantly longer, fuel prices in the city have tripled, and drivers risk their lives entering Taiz--all factors driving up food prices.
"High prices are inevitable now, but even at these rates, some buyers are willing to purchase everything we have. That is why we resorted to dividing wheat into five-kilogram bags and capping sales at one bag per person," the trader said.
Wheat and rice arriving at his store sell out the same day, he said, as residents gather in long queues the moment word spreads that a supply truck has reached the city.
The trader, who operates his own trucks, said that his drivers are reluctant to risk their lives crossing battle lines. "We only do this to help the people of Taiz, because everyone is terrified about what's coming and just wants safety," he said. "If not for that purpose, I would close my shop and stay home instead of risking my life to help others."
Ansarallah previously controlled the main roads leading into Taiz city between 2015 and 2016, before government forces advanced and secured the southern entrance road.
## **Taiz on the Frontline**
Taiz has been a major frontline between Ansarallah and government forces since 2015--when street battles in the city left civilians dead and injured. It endured a brutal, yearslong siege until a UN-brokered truce in 2022. That truce held across much of the country, including Taiz, until last month.
"We can manage the fuel crisis by using firewood for cooking and walking on foot instead of taking a bus, but our main concern now is the danger of battles reaching every home, as happened in 2015," Walid Saeed, a 51-year-old resident of Taiz city, told Drop Site.
Saeed lives with his wife, two children, and parents in Al-Moroor neighborhood of Taiz. Having lived through the 2015 battles in the city, he desperately wants to avoid repeating that nightmare and prefers to flee.
"I wish I could flee the city today, before tomorrow, but the roads aren't safe and fighting is ongoing. Fleeing right now means risking our lives, which is no different from staying," he said. "From a security standpoint, deciding to flee right now is not easy."
Saeed, who works as a daily-wage electrician, noted that fleeing the city also requires money to hire a vehicle--an expense that many people like him simply cannot afford.
"Unfortunately, we missed the window to flee safely, so we have no choice now but to stay in our home, even if the battles reach our doorstep," he said.
All public services in Taiz city have been impacted by the escalation: schools and universities are closed, and many public institutions have suspended operations until conditions stabilize. However, the most severe impact has been on health care, as the city serves as a critical medical hub for patients traveling from surrounding villages.
Ahmed Al-Issai, who is in his 60s, has suffered from kidney failure for more than five years. He used to travel twice a week from his village, 40 kilometers (about 25 miles) from Taiz city, for dialysis. But with the roads no longer safe, he has resorted to living in the courtyard of Al-Thawrah Hospital in Taiz city.
"There is no hospital outside the city that offers dialysis for my condition, and it isn't safe to keep traveling back and forth between my village and the hospital," Al-Issai told Drop Site. "I also cannot afford a hotel or a rented room because I am unemployed, so I resorted to sleeping on a piece of cardboard in this courtyard."
Al-Issai knows that if he misses or delays his dialysis sessions, he faces life-threatening complications. As a result, his entire life is now spent between that piece of cardboard and the dialysis machine, stepping away from the hospital yard only to find food.
"I won't leave the hospital courtyard until this escalation ends and the roads reopen," he said.
_NOTE: The reporter for this story has been granted anonymity because of the security situation in Yemen._

October 15, 2026. Photo by Khalid Al-Banna. TAIZ, Yemen--Like other residents of Taiz, Hael Mohammed is struggling to find food and other life essentials for his family as an escalating war between Ansarallah and a Saudi-led coalition draws in on the city. "No one can imagine how difficult the journey is just to find a propane cylinder or a bag of wheat in this city," the 41-year-old pharmacist and father of three told Drop Site News. "Many food traders told me their stores have run out of wheat, rice, and other essentials. When I finally found wheat, it was nearly double its normal price." Mohammed said that residents across Taiz are stockpiling food, fearing they could be trapped in their homes as the ground battles close in. The third largest city in Yemen, located in the southwestern highlands, Taiz has long been on the front line of Yemen's civil war--and is now encircled by fighting. Taiz governorate consists of 23 districts, 20 of which are now under Ansarallah control. Only three districts remain under control by the internationally recognized government--the three that comprise Taiz city itself. Ansarallah now controls all entry points to Taiz city. These entrances have turned into active frontlines with only brief pauses in fighting. Drivers are forced to wait for the short lulls--which usually last no more than a few hours a day--to enter or leave the city. The continuous fighting has sparked widespread terror among residents, who fear the conflict could reach their homes at any moment. The road blockades have also had severe economic consequences: fuel and basic commodities can no longer enter regularly, driving prices up to three times their normal cost for essential items like fuel. While some food trucks have managed to enter the city in recent weeks, supply has fallen far short of demand, with residents scrambling to stock up on supplies as the fighting rages on the outskirts. "The fighting is less than five kilometers (about 3 miles) from my home, and that is reason enough for me to be worried. I successfully purchased a 25-kilogram bag of wheat flour and I have cooking gas," Mohammed said. But he has been forced to go into debt to afford food. "That was the only way to secure food for my family," Mohammed said. "I went into debt even though I have a salary, so what about those who are unemployed or displaced? It must be much worse for them." For now he is buying bread from a local bakery, even though it costs 50% more than usual, preferring to preserve his cooking gas and flour rather than face another desperate search for supplies later on. "We won't use the gas until we are completely unable to leave our home," he said. A Growing Humanitarian Crisis Last month, Ansarallah (also known as the Houthis) swept south from their northern stronghold in a lightning offensive, launching heavy attacks on Saudi-backed government forces in southern Hodeidah and western Taiz governorate. The Houthis quickly took control of the strategic city of Mocha and Yemen's Red Sea coast to control the Bab al-Mandab strait, a vital waterway for global shipping. At the beginning of October, Ansarallah launched another major offensive against government forces in southern and western Taiz governorate. By October 4, they had made significant advances, seizing the main road linking Taiz city to the governorate's southern and western areas, as well as to Lahj governorate. The United Nations World Food Program (WFP) warned on Wednesday the fighting and road closures have cut off humanitarian assistance to some 800,000 people in Taiz and other affected areas. Wheat flour stocks are nearly exhausted, while remaining food supplies in local markets may last only a short time. In May, even before the latest phase of fighting, the UN warned that more than 22 million people required humanitarian assistance and protection services across Yemen, including 5.2 million who were displaced. The recent escalation in the military conflict has forced an additional 201,217 people from their homes, according to data released last week by the International Organization for Migration. The number is continuing to rise every day. Streets in Taiz city that used to be crowded late into the night are now largely deserted. As a result of the road closures into the city, the price of fuel has nearly tripled, with 20 liters (5.3 gallons) of petrol rising from 30,000 Yemeni riyals (around $19) to 90,000 riyals (around $57). Few cars and buses move through the streets by day, and almost none at night due to the security risks. | | ---|---|--- The normally bustling 26 September street in Taiz city is largely empty as residents stay indoors amid growing security concerns and a fuel crisis. October 2026. Photo by Khalid Al-Banna. Aside from the huge rise in transportation costs, getting food and other goods into the city has become a harrowing ordeal. "All the breadwinners went to the market at once to buy food, so it is only natural that our stores ran out," a food trader told Drop Site News. He agreed to speak on the condition of anonymity for security concerns. Several food traders declined to be interviewed about the crisis, fearing accusations of price gouging and hoarding from local residents. "There are drivers who wait sometimes for days for the fighting to pause--even if for just a few minutes or an hour--so they can enter the city with wheat, rice, or other supplies." The food trader said that deliveries take significantly longer, fuel prices in the city have tripled, and drivers risk their lives entering Taiz--all factors driving up food prices. "High prices are inevitable now, but even at these rates, some buyers are willing to purchase everything we have. That is why we resorted to dividing wheat into five-kilogram bags and capping sales at one bag per person," the trader said. Wheat and rice arriving at his store sell out the same day, he said, as residents gather in long queues the moment word spreads that a supply truck has reached the city. The trader, who operates his own trucks, said that his drivers are reluctant to risk their lives crossing battle lines. "We only do this to help the people of Taiz, because everyone is terrified about what's coming and just wants safety," he said. "If not for that purpose, I would close my shop and stay home instead of risking my life to help others." Ansarallah previously controlled the main roads leading into Taiz city between 2015 and 2016, before government forces advanced and secured the southern entrance road. Taiz on the Frontline Taiz has been a major frontline between Ansarallah and government forces since 2015--when street battles in the city left civilians dead and injured. It endured a brutal, yearslong siege until a UN-brokered truce in 2022. That truce held across much of the country, including Taiz, until last month. "We can manage the fuel crisis by using firewood for cooking and walking on foot instead of taking a bus, but our main concern now is the danger of battles reaching every home, as happened in 2015," Walid Saeed, a 51-year-old resident of Taiz city, told Drop Site. Saeed lives with his wife, two children, and parents in Al-Moroor neighborhood of Taiz. Having lived through the 2015 battles in the city, he desperately wants to avoid repeating that nightmare and prefers to flee. "I wish I could flee the city today, before tomorrow, but the roads aren't safe and fighting is ongoing. Fleeing right now means risking our lives, which is no different from staying," he said. "From a security standpoint, deciding to flee right now is not easy." Saeed, who works as a daily-wage electrician, noted that fleeing the city also requires money to hire a vehicle--an expense that many people like him simply cannot afford. "Unfortunately, we missed the window to flee safely, so we have no choice now but to stay in our home, even if the battles reach our doorstep," he said. All public services in Taiz city have been impacted by the escalation: schools and universities are closed, and many public institutions have suspended operations until conditions stabilize. However, the most severe impact has been on health care, as the city serves as a critical medical hub for patients traveling from surrounding villages. Ahmed Al-Issai, who is in his 60s, has suffered from kidney failure for more than five years. He used to travel twice a week from his village, 40 kilometers (about 25 miles) from Taiz city, for dialysis. But with the roads no longer safe, he has resorted to living in the courtyard of Al-Thawrah Hospital in Taiz city. "There is no hospital outside the city that offers dialysis for my condition, and it isn't safe to keep traveling back and forth between my village and the hospital," Al-Issai told Drop Site. "I also cannot afford a hotel or a rented room because I am unemployed, so I resorted to sleeping on a piece of cardboard in this courtyard." Al-Issai knows that if he misses or delays his dialysis sessions, he faces life-threatening complications. As a result, his entire life is now spent between that piece of cardboard and the dialysis machine, stepping away from the hospital yard only to find food. "I won't leave the hospital courtyard until this escalation ends and the roads reopen," he said. clean_body: I have to give you the harsh reality of where this race stands: the latest polling shows me trailing my opponent, "Dr. Lockdown" Amy Acton, by just three percentage points. | I'll be completely honest with you: asking for money is my least favorite part of this process. I would much rather be out on the trail, meeting voters and talking about our vision for a free society. But I have to give you the harsh reality of where this race stands: This race is a razor-thin, dead-heat battle. And the other side is raising MILLIONS to flip Ohio this November. | If you don't know my opponent, allow me to introduce you: As Ohio's Health Director during COVID-19, Amy Acton says she had to shut down outdoor county fairs because there was "no science for it." But she was totally fine allowing crowd-packed BLM protests to roil the streets at the same time. She wants you to forget that she is the architect of the devastating lockdowns that crushed Ohio's small businesses and kept our kids out of classrooms. Behind the polite facade is the exact same radical Left agenda: If she wins, Ohio becomes another testing ground for the radical Left's socialist policies - just look at Mamdani's New York and you'll understand their blueprint for Ohio. The only difference between Amy Acton and the Democrat Socialists elected in NY is that at least they're honest about where they stand. But if we win, we will abolish the state income tax, slash property taxes, protect our schools, and unleash unprecedented economic growth. | Please know that I never take your support for granted. And please, only give if this is a good time for you and your family. Your encouragement alone keeps us moving forward. In Liberty,Vivek G. Then, a poll dropped that shows us defeating Susan Collins by 1 point.

These are both the latest signs that our worker-first message is resonating with Mainers. It’s clear as day that after years of Susan’s kissing up to corporate interests, folks just want a government that works for them.

If we flip Maine, we can flip the Senate. I know we can win this seat and deliver a majority to Democrats. But if recent elections have shown us anything, it’s that **leads in the polls mean nothing, and election forecasters can be wrong.**

So it’s on us to fight like hell every day to send Susan Collins into retirement. But between the $60 million that she and her allies have amassed, and the billionaires at her beck and call, it won’t be easy.

Ultimately, in our district and around the country, we want the same things, like for working families to live in safe neighborhoods with reliable infrastructure, affordable goods, and quality jobs.
And it’s not easy in this environment of hate and division that extremists promote, but we have to always keep focus on the ones doing the work, not those yelling the loudest.
[**But the truth is we're seeing an uptick in spending by Republican super PACs seeking to divide our communities using nasty, misleading attacks. name: Public Land Warriors
subject: Hollow slogans won't save Montana's public lands
body:
We need clear action
We need clear action

| [|
---](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/VUcqhlCMBlXmCD9-5S4T0g~~/AAUS1hA~/PisTdXaV-bT9p2Zf0OnWx30lS8B-J5gbZvgZqEhriWe4nTbU94gFIi731sRixS1XXdqj61asRLtm8Gf8M7HxwQeM6nOhv65YoftsN0pmeyutbNMzBF7XhGJQ-2kpWIj8)
| | | | Peter, In Montana, 84% of voters oppose the sale or transfer of federal public lands. Everyone knows the rule:**if you openly admit you want to liquidate the backcountry, you get run out of the state on a rail.** So the politicians running for Montana's open House and Senate seats have memorized the standard script. Over the last week of debates, both Aaron Flint and Kurt Alme recited the exact same poll-tested talking point: _"keep public lands in public hands."_ It sounds great on a bumper sticker. But when you look at their actual records and the party platform they stand on, the reality is completely rotten. Here is what they refuse to say on the debate stage: **Aaron Flint** spent years on conservative talk radio advocating for transferring federal public lands to state control. He knows full well that transferring millions of acres to state balance sheets is the express lane to privatization when states can't afford wildfire suppression costs. And when pressed directly on the debate stage to pledge opposition to building massive AI data centers on federal lands, he dodged and refused to make the commitment. **Kurt Alme** claims he'll "fight anyone who tries to sell them off"—yet his campaign is actively being propped up by a Super PAC tied directly to the anti-federal land movement. He proudly touts Donald Trump's endorsement while Trump pushes to carve up 17,000 acres of Western public lands for tech conglomerates and roll back protections on 45 million acres of national forests. To top it all off, the Montana Republican Party's official platform explicitly supports transferring federal lands and leaves the door wide open to selling off public lands that aren't national parks or wilderness. They think repeating a four-word slogan will blind hunters, anglers, and hikers to the corporate giveaway they are preparing to vote for in Washington. [**They want to smile on stage and quietly rubber-stamp the sell-off in Congress. Will you pitch in $10 today to help us expose these hollow talking points before Election Day?**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/-3knEl-3VDwMAPRqDuhENQ~~/AAUS1hA~/nx---FCV9wYql7VmOrLKhWXMhftoX7OIDHQ2ca8btvhfFyxNtsJ48MbcS1qwQE9e0JVr_So_wBGHyHjI6yqaSkgEaFS4mn3k6DTNhw1waDGf-1ikycKxrNCkLPtMtqSl3lm81QixrqRtAeZ8WZl-eXdedSO7NpD_c0baSxyuVDWiHMlmlWkb79TqFLqoShOWHOP0njwFDcDbh2e6vVTUGUxrmnAC8i3Sdvi7Vo8FMA0EAnW_d7-zD5ra7keV3WDe) **[**DONATE »** ](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/7-Yd2GbNXNUA2ovuRdQqMQ~~/AAUS1hA~/ZnhB_v4K0GmdtTWlnGz_yFyV_v8NXOvxXFM5_QUW_YuJMHz3J6ZAlI--t3Bt_3lNvdKB9AnSO3chTbhhBdFlQNwblo-uzWvMfeX-yKYG22sTzGPuhQ3yejbyzBVg57oOUZn8Tp32cCxfMaajqUES1eGXHx7rgemv6KOASJvvVLhD2ypjiT8Jnj0HfC8jwyEH0F7qj_wLgxJxxM89p1p47KTGEponbar3jq9Ize2NJUtmDwsI9auEe7QxcuIaL4XD) ** You take our land—we take your seat. name: OnePA Team
subject: Demand impeachment for the Secretary overseeing ICE and DHS terror
body:
DHS raided a sitting member of Congress’s home. Tell Congress to begin impeachment proceedings against Secretary Markwayne Mullin. | |
---
Peter, ******DHS agents raided Rep. Ilhan Omar’s Washington home on October 12, just weeks before Election Day.** We must demand consequences for the Secretary overseeing a department that is bringing fear into our neighborhoods and is now attempting to intimidate a sitting member of Congress. Last month, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin publicly warned that something would happen to Rep. Omar. We see an administration escalating its attacks on a Black, Muslim congresswoman who refuses to bow to Trump. That intimidation reaches far beyond the Congresswoman’s doorstep. Our neighbors, organizers, and elected leaders must be free to challenge this administration without fearing federal agents at their door. **We are already seeing the violence Mullin is willing to defend. After ICE agents shot a man in New York with his 5-year-old son in the car, Mullin defended the agents and attacked the city’s immigration policies.** Families are living with the consequences of this violence and intimidation while the person responsible for overseeing DHS protects the agency from accountability. Our communities deserve safety, due process, and the freedom to organize. We cannot allow an authoritarian democracy where immigrant families fear federal agents and political opponents face intimidation from the government they challenge. **We’re demanding that Congress begin impeachment proceedings against Secretary Markwayne Mullin and investigate the abuses happening under his leadership.** [**Tell Congress to pursue Sec. Mullin’s impeachment, demand the records behind DHS’s raid on Rep. ****
**Republican Rep. Thomas Massie has already introduced articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.** Speaker Mike Johnson then sent the House home early, delaying consideration of that resolution until after the election. We have seen how congressional leadership can use the calendar to shield administration officials from a public vote.
We can put this demand directly in lawmakers’ offices while they are back in their districts asking for our votes. They should face clear questions about whether they support impeachment proceedings against Mullin, whether they will demand documents and testimony, and whether they will press leadership to act.
**OnePA members build power by bringing neighbors together, developing leaders, and holding elected officials accountable.** Black, immigrant, and working-class communities have every reason to organize together when federal power is used to make people afraid to speak, participate, or stand up for one another.
**Every message helps make our demand harder to ignore. We must press lawmakers to commit publicly, build support for impeachment proceedings, and keep the people harmed by DHS’s actions at the center of the fight for accountability.**

clean_body: DHS raided a sitting member of Congress’s home. Tell Congress to begin impeachment proceedings against Secretary Markwayne Mullin. | | Peter, ****DHS agents raided Rep. Ilhan Omar’s Washington home on October 12, just weeks before Election Day. We must demand consequences for the Secretary overseeing a department that is bringing fear into our neighborhoods and is now attempting to intimidate a sitting member of Congress. Last month, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin publicly warned that something would happen to Rep. Omar. We see an administration escalating its attacks on a Black, Muslim congresswoman who refuses to bow to Trump. That intimidation reaches far beyond the Congresswoman’s doorstep. Our neighbors, organizers, and elected leaders must be free to challenge this administration without fearing federal agents at their door. We are already seeing the violence Mullin is willing to defend. After ICE agents shot a man in New York with his 5-year-old son in the car, Mullin defended the agents and attacked the city’s immigration policies. Families are living with the consequences of this violence and intimidation while the person responsible for overseeing DHS protects the agency from accountability. Our communities deserve safety, due process, and the freedom to organize. We cannot allow an authoritarian democracy where immigrant families fear federal agents and political opponents face intimidation from the government they challenge. We’re demanding that Congress begin impeachment proceedings against Secretary Markwayne Mullin and investigate the abuses happening under his leadership. | | ** Republican Rep. Thomas Massie has already introduced articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Speaker Mike Johnson then sent the House home early, delaying consideration of that resolution until after the election. We have seen how congressional leadership can use the calendar to shield administration officials from a public vote. We can put this demand directly in lawmakers’ offices while they are back in their districts asking for our votes. They should face clear questions about whether they support impeachment proceedings against Mullin, whether they will demand documents and testimony, and whether they will press leadership to act. OnePA members build power by bringing neighbors together, developing leaders, and holding elected officials accountable. Black, immigrant, and working-class communities have every reason to organize together when federal power is used to make people afraid to speak, participate, or stand up for one another. Every message helps make our demand harder to ignore. We must press lawmakers to commit publicly, build support for impeachment proceedings, and keep the people harmed by DHS’s actions at the center of the fight for accountability.** Together, we will build power. -OnePA | OnePA is a 501(c)4 organization Contributions to OnePA are not tax deductible for federal income tax purposes Our mailing address is P.O. | | | My family and I were just at our temple in Aurora, Illinois. We recently learned that on the same day, a self proclaimed white supremacist attempted to commit a mass shooting at that very location.
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141508372/653780475/1090555623?refcode=261015_auroraincident&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhZjA3ZGVhZC1lMWM4LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=sVOciAwyXyEVT9uGvmx6lJXMzKeaTX5xl1ZntsmSESg=)
---
According to prosecutors, a 19-year-old man came to our temple intending to carry out a mass shooting of Indian Americans. He had 300 rounds of ammunition and an AR-15. When he went to open fire, his rifle jammed. He then went home to research online how to unjam an AR-15. He told a coworker what he had just done and his plans to carry out a massacre of innocent civilians. That coworker called the police. Officers arrested the shooter before he could return to the temple. It is hard to put into words the pain and fear this incident has caused on my local community, and on communities across America. Mostly, I’m thinking about every family who now has to wonder whether it’s safe to gather. I want to say thank you. To the coworker who didn’t look away. To the officers who acted immediately. They saved countless lives, and one of them is potentially mine. I won’t pretend this came out of nowhere. A recent report found a 240 percent surge in monthly anti-South Asian hate on X. A sitting Republican elected official has called for the mass deportation of Indians and called me a “foreign occupier.” Online hate, and hate perpetrated by elected officials and candidates for office to score cheap political points, does lead to fatal violence. Anti South Asian and anti Indian hate is on the rise. But this sort of violence affects all of us- women and LGBTQ+ persons. People of all races and ethnicities, and of all religions. Anyone who can be defined as “other” is harmed when we allow hate to proliferate. We cannot wait until innocent people are killed to take these threats seriously. **Every American deserves to live and worship without fear.** Today I called on the FBI to swiftly launch an investigation into this attempted mass shooting, and I will keep you updated on key developments. Thank you for standing with my family, and with every family that gathers to pray in peace. — Raja Krishnamoorthi

Friend, Whether you’re walking to the park or driving down the street, chances are you are being surveilled by Big Tech as well as local and federal law enforcement. Flock surveillance cameras now operate in over 5,000 communities across 49 states ― recording license plate numbers that are fed into a national database used by law enforcement. **Not only is this surveillance being used to help deport our immigrant neighbors, but police have also used Flock cameras to harass women (including ex-spouses), track patients who are receiving abortion care, and surveil people exercising their First Amendment rights.** In response to this surveillance state, I just introduced the **_Get the Flock Out of Our Communities Act_** , which prohibits federal funds from being used to purchase or operate any automated mass surveillance systems, including Flock license plate readers. It also requires state and local governments to drop Flock or related contracts in order to remain eligible for federal grants. **This is the only bill in Congress that completely prohibits federal funds from being used to purchase or run automated mass surveillance,** including facial recognition technology, which has been shown to falsely identify our residents because of the technology’s racist inaccuracies. [**Add your name as a grassroots co-signer of my new**** _Get the Flock Out of Our Communities Act_****and demand an end to the surveillance state.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39uDKkapQVnT18L0ER7M9Fm5KQTWkM5MtQVsbg7em64LdN7CU2m598zYGELP3uVSVv6km5MHo2BbTcjtG54eBaS2HBLlptjPqNC5tAW0H467_3kE5u3rHA76xlQQLxdHT_tWje8kMGIcfUNvVPxpyNhvcslErYw5vgoK9kPLY7ppfXzSVMrzt3NmJeVMc87ek7K4hqwo6i_A3DCz4ZBWiBtzm9wxeb6lAgrl7O3KDWnoCtHxzKNAj7uvRaT39YNXg5lHy2x3WjAfiyBbCvMrOdMgXeldBIdIj3k5KXkNouUVo1VC4AnEiZRER51poas1WGKMpQO9lH1CtsyA-tSlIJ3m6U20C1E9mxc40AtrHpOX5JQ_r4imTIM0v4cYGyKIhKpKWJS-etyxOmAa72h5y8i/4uw/NHEN2nwzT7uFVV7vCNEBlw/h1/h001.UAb7m08EhCM08raImQ5FlsbACfPp1vGr1fBZZD5HpEI) | [ADD YOUR NAME](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39uDKkapQVnT18L0ER7M9Fm5KQTWkM5MtQVsbg7em64LdN7CU2m598zYGELP3uVSVsc1UyowNGON_9rO78357TVin4xGszzTa3v30acbugLVMrC7GcE8y7H8kmLlrW12U5czbpWq_DZpFUwhg5ZCEVV3kHv2STZldA16ZSPghNWfWBz8zjvYYRfHm4D5jQs5SfzWrhDv4O2dKi2SghDM-3gZMbAdBIgf6TvUOjTG2LdxrlKhf2A7p-3q4fzhfTj-_7fP8DDnDunhmV_Ln455mbcjrXnCAm_0mHQBP95BcoI593vIopiAUeMP2ybZV_HKl4PHyvvKEtfCWh3pHgoWl5KoLp3HXzjUeeYR0sgsrbcRC8o2fYuEQfkBlxHKXvpkn5ocCMDErcvtrcXpzKMXoJs/4uw/NHEN2nwzT7uFVV7vCNEBlw/h2/h001.OPFXBaOKouLfxlmIywuPjwiVgW5RU_qYec9bP69o8-8)

Whether it’s a license plate reader that gets just one number wrong, resulting in law enforcement arresting the wrong person; whether it’s Big Tech using its surveillance technology to surveil protesters; whether it’s a law enforcement officer stalking a former spouse, **we are in the midst of a mass surveillance crisis and we need Congress to act to protect our rights.**

clean_body: We introduced this bill in my district in front of a Flock camera in Inkster, which just signed a long-term contract with Flock. | | | Friend, Whether you’re walking to the park or driving down the street, chances are you are being surveilled by Big Tech as well as local and federal law enforcement. Flock surveillance cameras now operate in over 5,000 communities across 49 states ― recording license plate numbers that are fed into a national database used by law enforcement. Not only is this surveillance being used to help deport our immigrant neighbors, but police have also used Flock cameras to harass women (including ex-spouses), track patients who are receiving abortion care, and surveil people exercising their First Amendment rights. In response to this surveillance state, I just introduced the Get the Flock Out of Our Communities Act , which prohibits federal funds from being used to purchase or operate any automated mass surveillance systems, including Flock license plate readers. It also requires state and local governments to drop Flock or related contracts in order to remain eligible for federal grants. This is the only bill in Congress that completely prohibits federal funds from being used to purchase or run automated mass surveillance, including facial recognition technology, which has been shown to falsely identify our residents because of the technology’s racist inaccuracies. | Whether it’s a license plate reader that gets just one number wrong, resulting in law enforcement arresting the wrong person; whether it’s Big Tech using its surveillance technology to surveil protesters; whether it’s a law enforcement officer stalking a former spouse, we are in the midst of a mass surveillance crisis and we need Congress to act to protect our rights. We introduced this bill in my district in front of a Flock camera in Inkster, which just signed a long-term contract with Flock ― against objections from the community. Surveillance technology is making us less safe, and its racist inaccuracies disproportionately harm Black and brown communities that are already at risk for over-criminalization. Thank you for joining me in demanding: Flock Out of Our Communities. | | Friend, Every dollar stolen from taxpayers is a dollar taken from the families, schools, and hospitals that need it. **No fraud is acceptable.** Not in Minnesota. Not in Florida. **Not anywhere.****
****
**That should be a simple rule. But in Washington, it isn’t.

I'll keep this brief.
Tomorrow is my last mid-month deadline before Election Day.
Tomorrow, voters across the Commonwealth and beyond will be watching to see if we can pull this off.
And in just 19 days from now, all our efforts can come to fruition when we retire Mitch McConnell and his corrupt legacy with him by defeating Andy Barr.
I'll never be able to express how grateful I am to all the ordinary people who set aside their hard-earned money because they believe in this movement. _Every single dollar raised from the campaign comes from people like you._
It never gets easier to ask for money, but I can't dress this up: **if we don 't hit this deadline, all of Andy Barr's attack ads against me will dominate the airwaves, and I won't be able to fight back.**
So please: if flipping this seat is worth even just $5, $10, $25 to you, will you step up before midnight tonight so I can keep pushing in this final stretch?
[Chip in to my Senate Campaign](https://substack.com/redirect/fdd0c81a-697a-4c8b-8218-230038fd0112?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

I owe it all to you.
Charles Booker

---|---|---
Friends,
From the moment I entered this race, I've been focused on one thing: putting the people of Kansas ahead of party and politics and finally giving them the kind of leadership they deserve.
Like thousands of Kansans across the state, I've watched Sen. Marshall spend his time in Washington backing policies that drive up prices for hard-working families, reduce access to healthcare and hurt our farmers and small-business owners -- all because he'd rather toe the party line than fight for the folks he was elected to represent.
I got into this race because it's time for things to change. It's time for Kansans to have a true champion. They deserve a leader who will listen to them, think critically about how to solve the challenges they're facing and stand up against the policies that hurt them -- even when doing so is hard.
I believe, with every fiber of my being, that the only way to create the kind of real change that Kansas and the country needs is for leaders to put party and politics aside and _listen to the people they represent_. It sounds like common sense, but it's an approach to politics that seems to have fallen out of practice in recent years. I'm running to change that. I'm not a politician. I haven't spent a decade in Washington. I'm a fifth-generation Kansan who loves my family, my community, my state and my country.
I'm fighting for those folks -- not corporate PACs or special interests. I'm in this for my granddaughter Stella and every other child in Kansas. I'm fighting for regular people who work hard to put food on the table, pay their mortgage and give their families the best life they possibly can. I'm here for every single Kansan who believes it's time to end the chaos and division, bring good Kansas values to Washington and make this country better than we found it. And, I'm in it for _**you.**_
Friends, I've met with thousands of Kansans who are ready for change. But with early voting having started, Sen. Marshall and his supporters are going all out to mislead voters about me and my record. The GOP's top super PAC just launched a massive ad buy to drown out our message, and it might be working: The latest polls show this race is tightening.
**I know we can win this, but only if we keep up our momentum and make sure we have the resources to respond to whatever Sen. Marshall and his supporters throw our way.**
**[So please, will you chip in anything you can to help us reach fight back against Sen. Marshall's attacks and flip this seat?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/6e437908-3cc1-46a2-aa30-aafacba84188?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Donate](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/6e437908-3cc1-46a2-aa30-aafacba84188?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Together, we can do this.
Thank you,
Adam

The midterms are less than a month away, and while everyone has their eyes trained on the House and Senate, a handful of highly contested gubernatorial races carry massive implications.
One of them is in Ohio... and something shocking is taking place.
For the first time in 20 years, a Democrat may win, but not for the reason you think.
Amy Acton vs. Vivek Ramaswamy. That's who's stepping up to the plate for both parties.
**[Kalshi odds](https://substack.com/redirect/92d7ac81-3830-42ad-96a6-d021b005beb1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** currently give Vivek Ramaswamy just a 31% chance of winning, despite Ohio going +11 points for Donald Trump in 2024. Vivek is struggling in recent polls after Amy Acton picked up an unlikely endorsement from Hitler apologist Nick Fuentes.
"Early voting has begun in Ohio. VOTE AMY ACTON FOR GOVERNOR," Fuentes said in a recent stream.

* * *
As early as May, he said the following: "We're gonna have to hold our noses and we're gonna have to vote Democrat. We have to deny Vivek Ramaswamy the governorship. I'll take an enemy over a traitor. We are going out for the Democrat happily, proudly as a middle finger to Vivek Ramaswamy and his giant head."
Both Fuentes and his supporters have made their motivations clear. They don't want to vote for someone who doesn't look like them, and they believe Vivek wants to import the Third World.
"You gave us Vivek, we'll give you Amy Acton, and no one is going to be happy about it. Do better next time."
Fuentes' reasoning is that if his base sides with Democrats this time, the GOP will listen to them next cycle and nominate someone "better."
While some Republicans have been receptive to this message, others, myself included, see a very different strategy at play.
Nick Fuentes doesn't want to change the GOP. He wants to destroy it.

Earlier this year, a leftist organization called the Southern Poverty Law Center (SPLC) was indicted for funding far-right extremist groups in an effort to manufacture extremism. Could this be another one of their campaigns?
We don't know for sure. But what we do know is that if it is, the polls show it's working.
Fuentes' logic is glaringly flawed. His camp assumes Vivek Ramaswamy wants to let the Third World in through legal immigration. Their solution? Elect an open-borders Democrat. They claim they won't vote for Ramaswamy because he's Hindu and doesn't share their faith, yet they are eager to elect a Democrat who hates their religion.
As the midterms come to a head, we have to ask ourselves the classic question once again: Is this all just internet noise? Will these people actually show up to vote? Or is it a sick alignment of the far-left and far-right working together to undermine MAGA and President Trump's agenda?

She came. She spoke. She delivered. | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141510497/653787878/-785282667?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1ZjYzOTc4Ni1lN2M4LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=RKIScrRXABK3RmoMNQiPPG9qf7rP3TDVmxh2dg-M6sA=)
---
Peter, **Yesterday, Becca welcomed a room FULL of women leaders from around the world to Vermont. And boy, did it make us proud.** The room was the W20 Summit, which gives women leaders and advocates a chance to help shape the economic priorities the G20 talks about. It was held at the Haskell Free Library and Opera House, a building that sits right on the border between Vermont and Quebec and was built to be shared by one community on both sides. Becca warmed up the room by sharing with everyone that teaching middle school, which she called a very spicy age group, was **“perfect preparation for the United States Congress.”** Hard to argue with someone who’s done both. **Then she got serious, the way she does best, and started talking about the people she’s thinking about when she walks into those rooms.** _She pictures a woman who runs a small farm and works from before sunrise until long after sunset, and still struggles to build savings._ _A young woman in a rural town who would make a great electrician but was never encouraged to consider it. _ _A mother who wants to go back to work and finds out child care costs more than she can even afford._ Then she brought the numbers. A report released this year found that Vermont women working full-time earn a median annual salary nearly $7,000 lower than their male counterparts. Becca put it in terms anybody can feel: **that’s the difference between paying the heating bill and having a cold house all winter.** [_**So here’s a different kind of ask. name: Ilhan Omar
subject: Bombshell report: Trump wants to take my citizenship.
body:
[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20261015-1-movement-split.Jkfn7j&refcode=em20261015-2828&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1001&akid=2828%2E342411%2E53Z2Pf ]Headline from THE WALL STREET JOURNAL: Ilhan Omar Investigation Aims to
Build Case for Stripping Her Citizenship.

Peter, I want
you to read just the first sentence of this bombshell report from the Wall
Street Journal:

“The Trump administration’s investigation into Rep. Ilhan Omar (D.,
Minn.) is aimed at building a case to strip her of her U.S. citizenship
and ultimately deport her, according to U.S. officials and other people
familiar with the probe.”

This is no longer just racist rhetoric — Trump’s fascist administration is
going to use every lever of power they hold to try to take away my
citizenship.

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20261015-1-movement-split.Jkfn7j&refcode=em20261015-2828&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=2828%2E342411%2E53Z2Pf ]Peter,
if you understand how serious this is and are ready to join me in fighting
back with everything we’ve got, rush a contribution between my campaign
and the Squad Victory Fund today to support my legal defense and help us
continue to organize against Trump’s authoritarian rule >>

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20261015-1-movement-split.Jkfn7j&refcode=em20261015-2828&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1003&akid=2828%2E342411%2E53Z2Pf ]Contribute ››

First, Trump spent years attacking me with racist insults while his
administration officials and allies in Congress spread baseless conspiracy
theories about me and my family, with the promise that I would be
investigated.

Then, Trump’s DHS agents raided and searched my home in a starkly
unprecedented and highly partisan move just weeks before the midterm
elections.

Now, subpoenas have been sent to my family members, and this new report
makes it clear that the administration’s ultimate goal is to take away my
citizenship and deport me. The raid on my house wasn’t the end of this —
it’s just the beginning of their escalations.

For years, Trump has broken so many laws and betrayed so many foundational
principles of our democracy. But we can’t grow numb to what’s happening
here. I’m one of Trump’s loudest critics. I oppose his warmongering, his
corruption, his greed, and I organize every day to defeat his violent
agenda.

This administration is trying to use the power of the federal government
to silence me and the entire movement we have built in opposition to his
failed presidency. That’s fascism, plain and simple, and we must fight
back.

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20261015-1-movement-split.Jkfn7j&refcode=em20261015-2828&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1004&akid=2828%2E342411%2E53Z2Pf ]I have been in awe of the incredible outpouring of support I’ve
received this week, and I’m hoping we can keep that momentum going.
Please, chip in whatever you can afford today, split between me and the
Squad Victory Fund, and help us fight back. From paying legal fees to
supporting candidates up and down the ballot, we will put every dollar we
raise to good use as we stand strong against Trump’s attacks.

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20261015-1-movement-split.Jkfn7j&refcode=em20261015-2828&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1023&akid=2828%2E342411%2E53Z2Pf ]Contribute ››

In solidarity,

Ilhan Omar

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way for us to reach you about opportunities to get involved. If you need to remove yourself from our email list, click here to unsubscribe:

You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:

Peter,
I prayed we would never reach this point.
I want to start with an apology.
Not for asking for your support -- but for the possibility that we may not have done enough to earn it.
If our House Majority is standing at the edge of what I'm about to describe, I want you to know I will carry the weight of that for the rest of my life.
[It's Congressman Brandon Gill. name: Governor Phil Scott
subject: Know Before You Vote, Vol. 3 ‘Getting By…’ without Federal Funds?
body:
|
---
| |
---
---
---
| **Know Before You Vote: Vol. 3**
**‘Getting By...’ without Federal Funds?**
My opponent has repeatedly talked about **_“reducing our reliance”_** on federal dollars.

Her argument is that using federal funds leaves Vermont vulnerable when federal priorities change... and while that’s a great soundbite, it doesn't add up or make any sense for Vermont.

**Vermonters should understand what that really means – and what impact that could have on our economy and our people. **

**_Federal funds account for more than $3.2 billion of our $9.19 billion state budget – roughly one-third of all of Vermont’s spending. _**

These dollars pay for healthcare, roads and bridges, rural broadband services, public transportation, education, disaster recovery, and more.

**So, let’s talk about transportation first:**

Vermont’s FY27 transportation program includes $515 million in federal funding, and $332 million in State Funds. The Federal dollars support interstate paving, public transit, and rail across Vermont.

Human services are also intertwined with federal funding, including, Vermont’s Global Commitment fund – which funds **Medicaid** and other healthcare programs for lower income households.

**Human services alone account for more than $2.2 BILLION, with the federal government providing a major share of the funding.**

So, if Vermont were to say “no thanks” to federal funding would we eliminate the programs completely or would we replace federal money with state tax revenue?

_**Which is it?**_

When I’m talking to folks across the state they tell me we should be doing more to improve our roads, not less. They want to make sure we take care of the most vulnerable, even though many of them are struggling to get by themselves.

**But they can’t afford to pay more in taxes, on that they’re clear.**

_So why would we run away from federal dollars and how would that make Vermont more affordable?_

Good questions.

**That’s worth knowing before you vote.**

Thanks -

clean_body: | | | | Know Before You Vote: Vol. 3 ‘Getting By...’ without Federal Funds? My opponent has repeatedly talked about “reducing our reliance” on federal dollars. Her argument is that using federal funds leaves Vermont vulnerable when federal priorities change... and while that’s a great soundbite, it doesn't add up or make any sense for Vermont. Vermonters should understand what that really means – and what impact that could have on our economy and our people. Federal funds account for more than $3.2 billion of our $9.19 billion state budget – roughly one-third of all of Vermont’s spending. These dollars pay for healthcare, roads and bridges, rural broadband services, public transportation, education, disaster recovery, and more. So, let’s talk about transportation first: Vermont’s FY27 transportation program includes $515 million in federal funding, and $332 million in State Funds. The Federal dollars support interstate paving, public transit, and rail across Vermont. Human services are also intertwined with federal funding, including, Vermont’s Global Commitment fund – which funds Medicaid and other healthcare programs for lower income households. Human services alone account for more than $2.2 BILLION, with the federal government providing a major share of the funding. So, if Vermont were to say “no thanks” to federal funding would we eliminate the programs completely or would we replace federal money with state tax revenue? Which is it? When I’m talking to folks across the state they tell me we should be doing more to improve our roads, not less. They want to make sure we take care of the most vulnerable, even though many of them are struggling to get by themselves. But they can’t afford to pay more in taxes, on that they’re clear. So why would we run away from federal dollars and how would that make Vermont more affordable? Good questions. That’s worth knowing before you vote. And he's not the only billionaire trying to tip the scales. These people are terrified of what will happen when we elect leaders who aren't beholden to them. While the Governor hogs the spotlight, he’s been quietly driving the extreme conservative agenda in the legislature for over a decade. Setting the agenda. Assigning committees. Strong-arming Senators into passing legislation that will hurt their districts. 4 days from now, early voting begins. I want to tell you 4 things about this race that don't usually make the headlines.
_**#1. He’s behind the sudden THC ban**_
Banning THC is one of Dan Patrick’s top priorities. After squabbling with the Governor last session (and losing), he’s gotten his way with a regulatory ban that took thousands of products off shelves overnight. Hundreds of small businesses are at risk of closing entirely.
I opposed the ban then, and I oppose it now. I want sensible rules that keep products away from kids, protect consumers, and let small business owners stay open.
Lt. Dan put it best: “I’m not going to legalize marijuana in Texas,” he said last year. “If people want to vote me out of office for that, so be it.” _Famous last words_.
_**#2. He doesn't want you to vote on the big stuff**_
Half the states in America let citizens propose ballot initiatives and have a direct voice in state law. Texas doesn't give us this power, and Dan Patrick likes it that way.
I filed the Empowering Texans Ballot Initiative Act to change that. Dan Patrick made sure that bill never even got a floor vote. He knows that if Texans were allowed to vote on hot-button issues directly, he wouldn’t like the results.
That's why he's blocking the question.
_**#3. He ignores the childcare crisis**_
Childcare centers across Texas are closing. Waitlists are years long. Working parents (especially moms) are making impossible choices.
I filed HB 4598 to help fund childcare programs through employer contributions. Dan Patrick didn't bring it to the floor because he doesn’t care – _the families waiting on those lists aren't his donors._
_**#4. A little girl named Cati drowned. I worked with her family to pass a law.**_
Drowning is the leading cause of death for young children in Texas.
In 2023, I worked directly with a family in my district who lost their daughter Cati to a drowning tragedy. Cati's Act requires childcare providers to have life jackets at pools for children who cannot swim.
**We need more laws that save lives, and more lawmakers working for their constituents.**
Dan's been in this office for 10 years. I'm asking: _what has he actually done for your family?_

Dan put it best: “I’m not going to legalize marijuana in Texas,” he said last year. “If people want to vote me out of office for that, so be it.” Famous last words. #2. He doesn't want you to vote on the big stuff Half the states in America let citizens propose ballot initiatives and have a direct voice in state law. Texas doesn't give us this power, and Dan Patrick likes it that way. I filed the Empowering Texans Ballot Initiative Act to change that. Dan Patrick made sure that bill never even got a floor vote. He knows that if Texans were allowed to vote on hot-button issues directly, he wouldn’t like the results. That's why he's blocking the question. #3. He ignores the childcare crisis Childcare centers across Texas are closing. Waitlists are years long. Working parents (especially moms) are making impossible choices. **Gina Hinojosa (TX Governor)** — A civil rights and labor attorney raised in Brownsville along the Texas-Mexico border, Gina is running to become Texas's first Latina governor — and the state's first Democratic governor since 1990. She got her start fighting to keep her son's elementary school open, and never stopped.
**JoAnna Mendoza (AZ-06)** — A proud Latina, Marine Corps veteran, and daughter of farmworkers who grew up working Arizona's cotton fields, JoAnna is running to flip one of the most competitive districts in the country. Her district is nearly 20% Hispanic or Latino — and she was the first candidate in the race to go up on air speaking directly to voters in both English and Spanish.
**Kristian Carranza (TX-HD118)** — A lifelong Southside San Antonio Latina raised by a single mother, Kristian is running for a Texas state house seat in a district where Latino voters are the majority. She's spent over a decade organizing in her community before ever deciding to run herself.
**Brenda Zamora (NV, Clark County School District)** — With four years under her belt on the Clark County school board—the same district her children attend—Brenda has worked tirelessly to bridge the gap between families and schools, ensuring every voice is heard. And as an immigrant daughter, she is deeply committed to protecting all our marginalized communities and making sure all families have a meaningful seat at the table.
The Latino vote is one of the fastest-growing forces in American politics, especially in states like Texas and Arizona, where it's already deciding elections. Candidates like Gina, JoAnna, Brenda, and Kristian aren't just representing their communities. They grew up in them, and they understand exactly what's at stake.
