Hey everyone, Matt the Angry Democrat here.
Trump just made a deal with Russia over diesel, and it has a lot of people confused. Democrats and Republicans are asking what we have been doing.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f84ac643-7189-42eb-b28a-12fa54bf293a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Russia invaded Ukraine. The United States and the European Union have been arming Ukraine to defend itself. We have sanctions on Russia. But now we're opening the door to Russian diesel to try to lower our fuel prices.
Buying that fuel gives Russia more money while it continues its war against the country we have been helping defend.
And the initial amount? A little more than half a day's worth of U.S. consumption.
So what is the strategy? Is this supposed to provide lasting relief, create a temporary price drop before the midterms, or pressure Zelenskyy into accepting a deal because we're now helping both sides?
Those are the possibilities I want to talk about, because the amount of fuel alone does not explain this decision.
* * *
## Understand the Scale of This War
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ec1f9114-f948-4df6-8a64-543a78425db8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Russia annexed Crimea in 2014. On February 24, 2022, it launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. That invasion is now in its fifth year, and we still do not have peace.
Russian strikes are hitting Ukrainian cities and infrastructure. Ukraine is striking Russian refineries and energy supply chains. We know this is happening, but I do not think enough people understand the scale.
The military death estimates are approximately 400,000 to 450,000 Russians and 125,000 to 150,000 Ukrainians. Combined military casualties, including those killed, wounded, or missing, were roughly two million.
That is more than half a million military deaths between the two countries.
And that does not include civilians. In Ukraine, July 2026 alone saw at least 437 civilians killed and 2,610 injured.
These are human beings. And when I think about the soldiers being sent into this, I think about ordinary people, poor people, people without the money or connections to insulate themselves from what their governments are doing.
The financial cost is astronomical, too. Russia's military spending in 2025 was approximately $190 billion. Ukraine's was about $84 billion. That is one year of military spending, not the entire cost of this war.
This is the scale we need to keep in mind when we talk about giving Russia another opportunity to earn money.
* * *
## North Korea Is Trading Human Lives for Money
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c6a87ecf-0083-420a-906d-68eee6df1150?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
One part of this conflict that I do not think gets enough attention is North Korea's involvement.
North Korea has been supplying Russia with troops, munitions, and missiles. I understand buying weapons from an ally. But the troops are what bother me.
In my opinion, this is an immoral trade of human life for money.
Russia needs more people to keep fighting. Another major mobilization carries the risk of unrest at home. North Korea can provide troops, and its government receives benefits for doing so.
To me, that amounts to treating people as a commodity. The government gets paid, and the soldiers get sent into a war.
North Korea's economy has benefited from its relationship with Russia. But I cannot look at those benefits without thinking about the people being shipped off to fight and whether they have any meaningful choice in the matter.
There is also the military experience. Having a large military and having a military tested in modern combat are different things. These deployments give North Korea experience it can take home.
So there are consequences here that extend beyond Russia and Ukraine. Money is changing hands, people are dying, and militaries are learning.
* * *
## The First Shipment Is Barely Half a Day's Worth
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ca702986-b3af-4713-88d0-a33162e7f7d7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Now look at what Trump announced.
The immediate supply is more than 300,000 metric tons of diesel. Then 500,000 tons in November, another million tons afterward, and an additional projected three million tons. The full announcement comes to approximately 4.8 million metric tons.
That sounds like a lot until you compare it with consumption.
Using a rounded U.S. consumption benchmark of about 526,000 metric tons per day for petroleum distillates, including diesel and heating oil:
* **The initial 300,000 tons:** About 14 hours of U.S. use.
* **November 's 500,000 tons:** About one day.
* **The following million tons:** About two days.
* **The entire 4.8 million tons:** About nine days.

And these announcements concern supply for U.S. and global markets. We cannot assume every ton is coming here.
This is why I keep coming back to the amount. We are easing restrictions on Russia for an initial shipment equivalent to a little more than half a day of American consumption.
Is that going to make a meaningful difference in our day-to-day lives? Is it going to provide lasting relief for fuel costs?
I am skeptical. The volume alone does not tell us exactly what prices will do, but it certainly makes me question the size of the benefit being promised.
Russia gets revenue from selling the fuel. What do we get, and for how long?
* * *
## Is the Plan to Dump It Into the Market Before the Midterms?
Here is one possibility: Maybe lasting relief is not the point.
Maybe the point is to get as much of this fuel into the market as possible right before the midterms and hope prices fall long enough to help Republicans.
Think about the timing. The initial 300,000 tons plus November's 500,000 tons would be approximately 800,000 tons. If those supplies became available before Election Day, could the administration try to concentrate the benefit into a very short window?
Could the goal be to push prices down for a few days, claim a victory, and get through the election?
I do not know whether that is the plan. But that is the strategy I am questioning.
There is a difference between fixing a supply problem and trying to produce a politically useful price drop at exactly the right moment. With quantities this limited, I can see why the timing might matter more to the administration than the long-term effect.
I am not claiming that releasing this amount would guarantee a dollar or two off the price. I am asking whether a short-lived reduction before people vote is what they are actually trying to achieve.
* * *
## Is This About Making Zelenskyy Capitulate?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/be4fcc61-8598-4553-bfb1-c08b18704f96?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy
The other possibility is that this is about pressuring Zelenskyy into accepting a deal.
We have been helping Ukraine defend itself against Russia. Now we are making it easier for Russia to earn money that can help sustain the war.
Imagine looking at that from Ukraine's position. You are already facing a larger country, years of destruction, and enormous losses. Now a country that has helped you defend yourself is opening another source of revenue for the country invading you.
Does that send the message that this could go on indefinitely unless you accept the terms being offered?
The message, as I see it, could be: We are going to help them, too. Give up the land they have taken, cut a deal, and call it a day.
That is my interpretation of a possible pressure tactic. I do not know that it is the administration's actual plan. But it is one way to understand a decision that otherwise seems to contradict what we have been supporting.
Maybe Trump thinks a stalemate is the only realistic outcome and wants to force Zelenskyy to the table. If so, is the method to make Ukraine's position worse until it capitulates?
That is a very different argument from telling Americans we are simply buying fuel to lower their costs.
* * *
## The Sanctions Exception Makes the Contradiction Clear
On October 9, the Treasury Department issued General License 135, temporarily permitting specified Russian diesel transactions through April 7, 2027.
So restrictions that were supposed to limit Russia's access to revenue are now being relaxed for this fuel.
Meanwhile, Ukraine has been attacking Russian refineries. Trump has pressed Ukraine to stop those attacks, and Zelenskyy has said Washington threatened consequences for intelligence sharing.
Russia continues attacking Ukraine's energy infrastructure, but we are trying to protect the flow of Russian diesel while helping Ukraine defend itself.
How does all of that fit together?
We also need clear answers about the transactions themselves. Who is buying the fuel? What is the price? How are payments being handled? How much will actually arrive, and when?
* * *
## Who Is Winning Here?
American taxpayers have funded military assistance. When we send weapons from our stockpiles, we also have to consider the cost of replenishing them. European allies have committed money and weapons, too.
Russia is spending enormous sums. Ukraine is fighting for its survival. North Korea is benefiting from supplying weapons and troops.
And now we are creating another opportunity for Russia to sell fuel.
So who is winning in this situation?
Trump said he would end this war on day one. We are approaching two years into his term, and instead of an end to the fighting, we are discussing a diesel deal with the country that launched the invasion.
The war itself is also changing how militaries fight. Drones, AI integration, fiber-optic controls, and satellite communications are all part of that conversation. The consequences will last far beyond whatever happens to fuel prices this month.
That is why I want people to understand the scale. If we do not understand the scale, we cannot understand the importance of these decisions.
My concern is that we are being sold a fuel-price explanation for something that may really be about election timing, pressure on Ukraine, or both.
**Do you agree with this deal?**
**Is a shipment equivalent to roughly half a day 's consumption worth easing restrictions on Russia? **
**And do you think the real goal is cheaper fuel, a political win before the midterms, or forcing Zelenskyy to accept a settlement?**
Right now, it looks like we are playing both sides. I want to know what the strategy is.

The time for deliberation is over.

| | A message from Senator Katie Britt
---
[Our 53-seat Majority is hanging by a single thread.](https://links.katiebrittforsenate.com/u/click?_t=64058844820c43dab0e6ed55204bc487&_m=f51d0b6e873746c4a45c5847ea49caea&_e=N1CVEEKiolkoEUXf69t8es4JflSXYdRPOH0r1kqsCz3bTxsTpEOaYKZrmMZG35mxai8dKD6o5fTm9sImnlXTuHSj6KO7d3hb2O5sJP3I8rJytVPM0hP419D6FV1cMT7iLCfqNENdXUQTaVEQM_I-jmHxpe2rGLMvs-G_GkCeBLMAz-R04fi9XiHXGnucplAv5G0CpY_F_2FHLAcTiubVpD2_7Io5g0qW4rvGJicWAAUzILGlFnY65uIRsmvsR1wXS4QFqN6hPsx8ZvysG-58ZV6pKk4V2PLC3FQEIhbP9TCyijDXdPSd0N4pvMPEIlYFdICV7_YX3iDzrnIIl0ZJzJGRH-gB8yMqwm35p9d0zxeBLxRbJ3KYc7IaRrzPV_aIJqIY7zuU0X_qUhBPwkN4hFWp3zrkmpq5zHY2ZJJWQrtd4FYSuWRbJgJvuMST17i_eoGTbhzosB_u33_LvsmGk4Oza7tL6HCqfnyY0uUbHfUsUf0c9VGUyw59BlBr9TBe_iqNxLYIe2rlxJ1WfMF4STvolzDsfEEOmmVAtAI9Mvms47EM7NtYF4B9nXdTYy-ymvbyzN36yQuhVQsWhlwXgz_2sReepNTyx9BZ3bGM55MGFkrfgN0_jHV0DuXePWyElunQTz4fb4a-wNjXnvDqg5XFbMIT5i-aXhAaaldaG1YIYXPXZpjP5XFkhMTRQeI76xVrAKaT5FQiE4DkT-zR4lxwq_i4i37Pf5bRwM1rdf6Mf60YIRY3lHENWtRygD-vz35mmrXDicCHBwhukRKUruX-MqscnN9aGVQfNl4boq9Z-aJY3nkFqUvos4Vz7RZlxxF-G3L10HcISt2HsL_P6pX6xFgvh8WDp6UfxcFRTm6KuR2njQnhiHJE0BeRduSG)
Peter – I’m writing this with a heavy heart because, to be honest, I feel like I’m at a complete loss. Today, we had a briefing on our October fundraising numbers, and the threat we’re facing is _**_heartbreaking_**_. subject: Greg Abbott’s empty podium
body:
I was at his front door at 10 a.m. He wouldn’t come out.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, this morning at 10 a.m., I stood outside the Governor’s Mansion, ready to debate Greg Abbott.
He didn’t show up.
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261015_3_podium.CjIgIt&refcode=em20261015-2439&amount=5&t=1&akid=2439%2E299639%2EgoGM0d)
I told Abbott that if he’s not man enough to debate me, he doesn’t deserve to be Governor of Texas. Today he answered with an empty podium, at a debate held right outside his own front door.
**He doesn’t want to answer for his record of putting wealthy donors and corporate interests ahead of Texans. So instead of facing the music, he’s hiding.**
There are only 19 days left in this campaign, and early voting starts Monday. This race is razor-thin: six polls in the last month have shown us ahead. But polls don’t vote. We need Texans to actually turn out, and that takes resources.
We need to fund TV ads, digital outreach, and get-out-the-vote events across Texas in these final weeks. We can’t do any of it without your support.

body:
| Friend,

I hope you’re well! I’m reaching out because I know how much you care about helping Democrats take back the House Majority.

Democratic candidates across the country are hitting the ground in their districts and working tirelessly to communicate their message to voters in order to win in November and deliver for the American people in Congress.

Through the Red Alert program, the DCCC is highlighting Frontline Members and Red to Blue candidates in some of the tightest races in the country. With less than 30 days until Election Day, **_[they need your help.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141513590/653798111/-1911020574?refcode=ab&source=EM_NBI_AB_20261015_FR_RedAlert_0_6MO_AmiBera_NA_NA_RedAlert&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS85MDU3OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5ODI3MDc3ZS1mMGM4LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=YJW5MB6IUMyJvTXsnrxZuNFMCj1wZz0DkboFM5HwP-c=)_**
_DCCC Red Alert Round #3
**Frontline Members:**_
Rep. Susie Lee (NV-03)
Rep. Tom Suozzi (NY-03)
Rep. Marcy Kaptur (OH-09)

**Red to Blue Candidates:**
Chris Jones (AR-02)
Amish Shah (AZ-01)
Manny Rutinel (CO-08)
Pia Dandiya (FL-22)
Cait Conley (NY-17)
Bob Harvie (PA-01)
Nancy Lacore (SC-01)
Mitchell Berman (WI-01)
Republicans know that **Susie Lee (NV-03), Tom Suozzi (NY-03) and Marcy Kaptur (OH-09)** won’t be easy to beat, so Donald Trump and Republican super PACs are spending millions against them. They need the resources to continue fighting back and communicating with voters in their districts.

**Chris Jones (AR-02)** was just added to the DCCC Red to Blue list, because he has put this traditionally Republican seat on the map. Chris is a 7th-generation Arkansan raised by parents who were both ministers. He has what it takes to win in November and flip this seat blue.

**Dr. Amish Shah (AZ-01)** is an emergency room physician who came within just 4% of flipping this district in 2024 – one of the closest margins of the cycle. Now an open seat, this is one of Democrats’ top pick up opportunities in 2026.

**Manny Rutinel (CO-08)** is running in one of the most competitive House districts in the country. The son of a single mom who immigrated from Latin America, Manny is running hard through the finish line as everyday Coloradans grow even more sour on Gabe Evans and Donald Trump’s disastrous agenda.

A working mom, educator and Palm Beach native, **Pia Dandiya (FL-22)** represents the people-first values that Congress needs while her self-funder opponent has endorsed Trump’s cost-spiking tariffs and the One Big Ugly Bill. This district was redrawn by corrupt Florida Republicans to benefit the GOP, but Pia is putting the seat in reach.

**Cait Conley (NY-17)** is running against one of only _three_ Republicans in a Congressional district that Kamala Harris won in 2024. Cait is a combat veteran who is ready to win this seat in November and retire Trump Republican Mike Lawler.

In another seat that Kamala Harris won last cycle, Republicans have spent over $3 million dollars attacking **Bob Harvie (PA-01)** , but poll after poll shows that this race is in a dead heat.

**Nancy Lacore (SC-01)** served our nation for 35 years in the Navy, a career that began as a helicopter pilot and culminated as a three star admiral and the Chief of Navy Reserve where she was entrusted to lead more than 60,000 sailors. Now, Nancy is running for Congress in SC-01, in a race she can win if she has the resources to communicate and get out the vote.

**Mitchell Berman (WI-01)** is uniquely positioned to flip this district in November. As an ER nurse who has seen firsthand how patients struggle to get care because of Republican policies, Mitch is committed to standing up to corruption and special interests in Washington.
**[Could you donate now to support these 11 candidates and help take back the House?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141513591/653798113/-1911020574?refcode=ab&source=EM_NBI_AB_20261015_FR_RedAlert_0_6MO_AmiBera_NA_NA_RedAlert&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS85MDU3OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5ODI3MDc3ZS1mMGM4LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=YJW5MB6IUMyJvTXsnrxZuNFMCj1wZz0DkboFM5HwP-c=)**
Thank you for all you do to help House Democrats. Together, we can take back the House Majority, and continue our fight to improve the lives of all Americans.

All my best,
Dr. Ami Bera

People like me belong in Minnesota, in America, and in Congress
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2529%2E791427%2EQ3xRmA)

Friend, with my family and my name being dragged through the mud by Trump and the right-wing media right now, I want to take a moment to tell you my story.
I was born in Somalia at the start of a brutal civil war. My mother died when I was just two. My family fled the country and spent four long years living in a refugee camp in Kenya.
Everything changed when we were granted asylum in America — an opportunity for a fresh start. But once we got here, we barely had a penny to our name. It wasn’t easy to get by.
I started cleaning office buildings, and throughout high school and college, worked as a cashier, security guard, educator, and policy analyst to make ends meet.
Throughout my upbringing in America, I faced harassment for my religion, my hijab, my race, my accent — you name it. But I found a wonderful home and community here in Minneapolis. I got involved locally and started organizing with my neighbors. In 2018, I ran for Congress and, along with Rashida Tlaib, became the first Muslim woman to serve in this historic body.
**I know my story — and none of the lies and conspiracy theories that Trump and MAGA come up with will change that.**
I’ve survived civil war, refugee camps, and the long process to become a proud American. Trump can lie about me. He can send DHS to raid my home. He can subpoena my family. He can try to take away my citizenship.
**But if Trump thinks I will be intimidated or silenced by these fascist tactics, he doesn’t know who the hell he’s messing with.**
[**Friend, with just days to go until the hugely consequential midterm elections, I’m going to do everything I can to take back Congress from MAGA so we can stop Trump’s lawless corruption. During last week’s debate, I confronted my opponent, John Braun, about his despicable vote against legislation designed to protect children from sexually explicit content generated by AI chatbots. His response? He accused me of lying and claimed the bill didn't even exist. Then the Seattle Times confirmed exactly what I said:
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141514106/653799776/-995582223?refcode=261015-debate-factcheck&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTkyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhMWMzOGJmNi1mM2M4LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=z4BFyv7FtbpyOnI4XD0yR1cwLoPubij83FxDDDIxGVQ=)

John Braun was one of just five state senators to vote against the bill. Here's what that legislation actually does: It requires technology companies to take reasonable steps to prevent AI companion chatbots from generating sexually explicit content or engaging in sexually suggestive conversations with children. It also requires safeguards to limit the development of emotional relationships between kids and these chatbots. **These are basic protections for our children in a world where technology advances faster than parents can keep up.****_And John Braun voted against them._** When I asked him to explain that vote in front of voters, he didn't defend his position or offer his own perspective. He lied to all of our faces. _The very next day, his campaign was forced to walk back that denial._ **Look, I don't expect everyone to agree with me on every issue. But protecting our kids from sexually explicit material online shouldn't be controversial. And neither should telling voters the truth about your record.** We're less than three weeks from Election Day, and this race is effectively tied. clean_body: Braun voted against restricting AI chatbots from sending sexually explicit material to minors| | | | = During last week’s debate, I confronted my opponent, John Braun, about his despicable vote against legislation designed to protect children from sexually explicit content generated by AI chatbots. His response? He accused me of lying and claimed the bill didn't even exist. Then the Seattle Times confirmed exactly what I said: = John Braun was one of just five state senators to vote against the bill. Here's what that legislation actually does: It requires technology companies to take reasonable steps to prevent AI companion chatbots from generating sexually explicit content or engaging in sexually suggestive conversations with children. It also requires safeguards to limit the development of emotional relationships between kids and these chatbots. These are basic protections for our children in a world where technology advances faster than parents can keep up.And John Braun voted against them. When I asked him to explain that vote in front of voters, he didn't defend his position or offer his own perspective. He lied to all of our faces. The very next day, his campaign was forced to walk back that denial. Look, I don't expect everyone to agree with me on every issue. But protecting our kids from sexually explicit material online shouldn't be controversial. And neither should telling voters the truth about your record. We're less than three weeks from Election Day, and this race is effectively tied. Donald Trump and Republican outside groups are spending millions of dollars to elect John Braun, and we're facing a multimillion-dollar spending disadvantage. We cannot let John Braun and his allies spend their way out of accountability. = = | | | John Braun can try to rewrite history, but his vote is on the record, and the people of Southwest Washington deserve to know about it.
